sentences.zh: 劉琨

translations.literal: Liu Kun.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Kun

sentences.zh: 劉琨，字越石，中山魏昌人，漢中山靖王勝之後也。

translations.literal: Liu Kun, courtesy name Yueshi, was a man of Weichang in Zhongshan, a descendant of Han Prince Jing of Zhongshan, Sheng.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Kun, courtesy name Yueshi, came from Weichang in Zhongshan and traced his line to Prince Jing of Zhongshan under the Han.

sentences.zh: 祖邁，有經國之才，爲相國參軍、散騎常侍。

translations.literal: His grandfather Mai had talent to order the state and served as army adviser to the minister of state and gentleman of the household for all purposes.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Liu Mai was a statesman who served as army adviser to the minister of state and gentleman for all purposes.

sentences.zh: 父蕃，清高沖儉，位至光祿大夫。

translations.literal: His father Fan was lofty, pure, retiring, and frugal, reaching office as grand master of splendid carriage.
translations.idiomatic: His father, Liu Fan, was austere and modest, rising to grand master of splendid carriage.

sentences.zh: 琨少得俊朗之目，與范陽祖納俱以雄豪著名。

translations.literal: Kun in youth gained the appraisal of handsome clarity, and together with Zu Na of Fanyang was famed for heroic dash.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he was hailed as brilliant and bold, and stood with Zu Na of Fanyang among the age’s boldest spirits.

sentences.zh: 年二十六，爲司隸從事。

translations.literal: At age twenty-six he became an attendant clerk under the metropolitan commandant.
translations.idiomatic: At twenty-six he entered service as an attendant clerk under the metropolitan commandant.

sentences.zh: 時征虜將軍石崇河南金谷澗中有別廬，冠絕時輩，引致賓客，日以賦詩。

translations.literal: At the time General Who Conquers the Barbarians Shi Chong had a separate villa in the Gold Valley ravine south of the river in Henan, surpassing his contemporaries; he drew in guests and each day composed poetry.
translations.idiomatic: General Shi Chong kept a villa in Henan’s Gold Valley gorge that outshone every rival salon of the day, where he gathered literati for daily verse-making.

sentences.zh: 琨預其間，文詠頗爲當時所許。

translations.literal: Kun took part among them; his writings were much praised by the age.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Kun joined their circle, and his poems won wide acclaim.

sentences.zh: 秘書監賈謐參管朝政，京師人士無不傾心。

translations.literal: Director of the Palace Library Jia Mi participated in governing court affairs, and gentlemen of the capital none did not incline their hearts toward him.
translations.idiomatic: When Jia Mi ran the palace library and politics together, the Luoyang elite flocked to his faction.

sentences.zh: 石崇、歐陽建、陸機、陸雲之徒，並以文才降節事謐，琨兄弟亦在其間，號曰「二十四友」。

translations.literal: Shi Chong, Ouyang Jian, Lu Ji, Lu Yun, and their sort all lowered their integrity with literary talent to serve Mi; Kun and his brothers were also among them, called the Twenty-Four Friends.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Chong, Ouyang Jian, the Lu brothers, and others lent their literary fame to Jia Mi’s salon; the Liu brothers were numbered among the so-called Twenty-Four Friends.

sentences.zh: 太尉高密王泰辟爲掾，頻遷著作郎、太學博士、尚書郎。

translations.literal: Grand Commandant the Prince of Gaomi, Tai, summoned him as an attendant clerk; by successive promotions he reached editorial director, erudite of the imperial academy, and gentleman of the masters of writing.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Sima Tai of Gaomi took him on staff; he rose to editorial director, imperial academy erudite, and gentleman of the masters of writing.

sentences.zh: 趙王倫執政，以琨爲記室督，轉從事中郎。

translations.literal: When Prince Zhao of Lun held power, he made Kun recorder-in-chief supervisor, then transferred him to staff supervisor.
translations.idiomatic: When Sima Lun, Prince of Zhao, seized the government, Liu Kun became recorder-in-chief supervisor, then staff supervisor.

sentences.zh: 倫子荂，即琨姊婿也，故琨父子兄弟並爲倫所委任。

translations.literal: Lun’s son Fu was none other than Kun’s sister’s husband; therefore Kun’s father, sons, and brothers were all entrusted by Lun.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Lun’s son Sima Fu was Liu Kun’s brother-in-law, so the whole Liu family served Lun’s regime.

sentences.zh: 及篡，荂爲皇太子，琨爲荂詹事。

translations.literal: When Lun usurped, Fu became crown prince and Kun became Fu’s household supervisor.
translations.idiomatic: When Lun took the throne, Sima Fu became crown prince and Liu Kun his household supervisor.

sentences.zh: 三王之討倫也，以琨爲冠軍、假節，與孫秀子會率宿衞兵三萬距成都王穎，戰于黃橋，琨大敗而還，焚河橋以自固。

translations.literal: When the three princes punished Lun, they made Kun General Who Crowns the Army with credential staff; together with Sun Xiu’s son Hui he led thirty thousand palace guards against the Prince of Chengdu, Ying, fought at Yellow Bridge, Kun was greatly defeated and returned, and burned the river bridge to secure himself.
translations.idiomatic: During the coalition against Sima Lun, Liu Kun was named General Who Crowns the Army and, with Sun Hui and thirty thousand guards, faced Sima Ying at Yellow Bridge; routed, he burned the bridge to stem pursuit.

sentences.zh: 及齊王冏輔政，以其父兄皆有當世之望，故特宥之，拜兄輿爲中書郎，琨爲尚書左丞，轉司徒左長史。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Qi, Jiong, assisted the government, because his father and elder brothers all had renown in the age, therefore he especially pardoned them, appointed elder brother Yu as gentleman of the palace secretariat, Kun as left assistant in the masters of writing, then transferred to chief clerk of the left under the minister of education.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Jiong spared the Lius for their prestige, named Liu Yu gentleman of the palace secretariat, Liu Kun left assistant in the masters of writing, then chief clerk on the minister of education’s left.

sentences.zh: 冏敗，范陽王虓鎮許昌，引爲司馬。

translations.literal: When Jiong was defeated, the Prince of Fanyang, Xiao, garrisoned Xuchang and brought him in as major.
translations.idiomatic: After Sima Jiong fell, Sima Xiao, Prince of Fanyang, who held Xuchang, took Liu Kun on as his major.

sentences.zh: 及惠帝幸長安，東海王越謀迎大駕，以琨父蕃爲淮北護軍、豫州刺史。

translations.literal: When Emperor Hui went to Chang’an, the Prince of Donghai, Yue, plotted to welcome the Grand Carriage and made Kun’s father Fan defender north of the Huai and inspector of Yu province.
translations.idiomatic: While Emperor Hui was in Chang’an, Sima Yue named Liu Fan defender north of the Huai and inspector of Yu province as part of a plan to restore the court eastward.

sentences.zh: 劉喬攻范陽王虓於許昌也，琨與汝南太守杜育等率兵救之，未至而虓敗，琨與虓俱奔河北，琨之父母遂爲劉喬所執。

translations.literal: When Liu Qiao attacked the Prince of Fanyang, Xiao, at Xuchang, Kun together with Administrator of Runan Du Yu and others led troops to rescue him; before they arrived Xiao was defeated; Kun together with Xiao both fled to north of the river; Kun’s father and mother thereupon were seized by Liu Qiao.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Qiao struck Sima Xiao at Xuchang, Liu Kun marched with Du Yu of Runan to relieve him but arrived too late; fleeing north with Xiao, he lost his parents to Liu Qiao’s captors.

sentences.zh: 琨乃説冀州刺史溫羨，使讓位於虓。

translations.literal: Kun then persuaded Inspector of Ji province Wen Xian to yield his post to Xiao.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Kun persuaded Ji province’s Wen Xian to step aside for Sima Xiao.

sentences.zh: 及虓領冀州，遣琨詣幽州，乞師于王浚，得突騎八百人，與虓濟河，共破東平王懋於廩丘，南走劉喬，始得其父母。

translations.literal: When Xiao took Ji province, he sent Kun to You province to beg troops from Wang Jun, obtained eight hundred raiding horsemen, crossed the river with Xiao, together broke the Prince of Dongping, Mao, at Linqiu, drove Liu Qiao south, and only then recovered his parents.
translations.idiomatic: Once Sima Xiao held Ji province, Liu Kun went to Wang Jun for eight hundred horsemen, recrossed the Yellow River, defeated Sima Mao at Linqiu, drove Liu Qiao back, and ransomed his parents.

sentences.zh: 又斬石超，降呂朗，因統諸軍奉迎大駕于長安。

translations.literal: He further beheaded Shi Chao, accepted Lu Lang’s surrender, and thereupon commanded the hosts to welcome the Grand Carriage at Chang’an.
translations.idiomatic: He cut down Shi Chao, accepted Lu Lang’s surrender, and led the allied armies to escort the emperor in Chang’an.

sentences.zh: 以動封廣武侯，邑二千戸。

translations.literal: By merit he was enfeoffed Marquis of Guangwu with two thousand households’ fief.
translations.idiomatic: For these services he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Guangwu with a two-thousand-household fief.

sentences.zh: 尋拜並州刺史，加振威將軍，領匈奴中郎將。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed inspector of Bing province, added General Who Rouses Might, and concurrent leader of courtiers of the Xiongnu.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon named inspector of Bing province with the added titles General Who Rouses Might and Xiongnu leader-of-court.

sentences.zh: 琨在道屢上表陳請，朝廷多從之。

translations.literal: While en route Kun repeatedly submitted memorials of request; the court for the most part granted them.
translations.idiomatic: On the march he petitioned repeatedly and the court largely approved.

sentences.zh: 時東嬴公騰自晉陽鎮鄴，并土饑荒，百姓隨騰南下，餘戸不滿二萬，寇賊繼橫，道路斷塞。

translations.literal: At the time Duke Dongying, Teng, moved from Jinyang to garrison Ye; Bing soil was famine-stricken; common people followed Teng south; remaining households were fewer than twenty thousand; bandits succeeded one another in ravaging and roads were blocked.
translations.idiomatic: Duke Sima Teng of Dongying had shifted from Jinyang to Ye, leaving Bing a wasteland: fewer than twenty thousand souls remained, bandits ruled the roads, and famine stalked the province.

sentences.zh: 琨募得千餘人，轉鬪至晉陽。

translations.literal: Kun recruited more than a thousand men and fought his way through to Jinyang.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Kun scraped together a thousand fighters and battled his way into Jinyang.

sentences.zh: 府寺焚毀，僵屍蔽地，其有存者，饑羸無復人色，荊棘成林，豺狼滿道。

translations.literal: Yamens were burned and ruined, stiff corpses covered the ground; those who survived were famished and wasted beyond human color; brambles became forests and wolves filled the roads.
translations.idiomatic: The city was charnel ground: ruined offices, corpses stacked deep, survivors gaunt as ghosts, brambles choking the streets and wolves prowling at noon.

sentences.zh: 琨翦除荊棘，收葬枯骸，造府朝，建市獄。

translations.literal: Kun cut away brambles, gathered and buried the dry bones, built a headquarters, and set up markets and prisons.
translations.idiomatic: He cleared the scrub, buried the dead, rebuilt a seat of government, and restored markets and jails.

sentences.zh: 寇盜互來掩襲，恆以城門爲戰場，百姓負楯以耕，屬鞬而耨。

translations.literal: Bandits raided in turn; always they made the city gates their battlefield; commoners shouldered shields to plough and girded quivers to weed.
translations.idiomatic: Raiders struck again and again at the gates; farmers tilled with shields on their backs and weeded with quivers at their belts.

sentences.zh: 琨撫循勞徠，甚得物情。

translations.literal: Kun comforted, followed up, and consoled arrivals, and greatly won the people’s hearts.
translations.idiomatic: His care for refugees won him deep loyalty among the people.

sentences.zh: 劉元海時在離石，相去三百許里。

translations.literal: At the time Liu Yuanhai was at Lishi, separated by about three hundred li.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yuan lay at Lishi, only some three hundred li away.

sentences.zh: 琨密遣離間其部雜虜，降者萬餘落。

translations.literal: Kun secretly sent agents to sow discord among his mixed barbarian followers; those who surrendered were more than ten thousand camps.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Kun’s agents peeled away more than ten thousand barbarian camps from Liu Yuan’s coalition.

sentences.zh: 元海甚懼，遂城蒲子而居之。

translations.literal: Yuanhai was greatly afraid, then walled Pu and dwelt there.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yuan grew alarmed and moved his capital into fortified Pu.

sentences.zh: 在官未期，流人稍復，雞犬之音復相接矣。

translations.literal: Before a full year in office, displaced people gradually returned; the sounds of chickens and dogs again joined one another.
translations.idiomatic: Within a year refugees trickled back until dogs barked and cocks crowed again across the land.

sentences.zh: 琨父蕃自洛赴之。

translations.literal: Kun’s father Fan came from Luoyang to join him.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Fan left Luoyang to join his son.

sentences.zh: 人士奔迸者多歸於琨，琨善於懷撫，而短於控御。

translations.literal: Gentlemen who fled in panic mostly turned to Kun; Kun was good at cherishing and soothing them but poor at controlling them.
translations.idiomatic: Fugitive gentry rallied to Liu Kun, who welcomed them warmly yet could not hold them in discipline.

sentences.zh: 一日之中，雖歸者數千，去者亦以相繼。

translations.literal: Within a single day, although thousands returned, leavers also followed one after another.
translations.idiomatic: In one day thousands might arrive—and hundreds depart again.

sentences.zh: 然素奢豪，嗜聲色，雖暫自矯勵，而輒復縱逸。

translations.literal: Yet by nature he was extravagant and proud, addicted to music and women; although he briefly restrained himself, again he would give way to excess.
translations.idiomatic: He was by nature lavish and sensual; bursts of self-discipline soon collapsed into old excesses.

sentences.zh: 河南徐潤者，以音律自通，游於貴勢，琨甚愛之，署爲晉陽令。

translations.literal: Xu Run of Henan, who by musical pitch made himself understood, wandered among the mighty; Kun greatly loved him and appointed him magistrate of Jinyang.
translations.idiomatic: A Henan musician named Xu Run curried favor with the great; Liu Kun doted on him and named him magistrate of Jinyang.

sentences.zh: 潤恃寵驕恣，干預琨政。

translations.literal: Run relied on favor to be arrogant and wanton and meddled in Kun’s government.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Run abused Liu Kun’s favor and meddled in administration.

sentences.zh: 奮威護軍令狐盛性亢直，數以此爲諫，並勸琨除潤，琨不納。

translations.literal: General Who Displays Might protector Linghu Sheng by nature was bluntly upright and several times remonstrated on this score, together urging Kun to remove Run; Kun did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: The blunt protector Linghu Sheng urged Liu Kun repeatedly to be rid of Xu Run; Liu Kun refused.

sentences.zh: 初，單于猗迤以救東嬴公騰之功，琨表其弟猗盧爲代郡公，與劉希合眾於中山。

translations.literal: Earlier, the Shanyu Yiyi for merit in rescuing Duke Dongying, Teng, had Kun memorialize his younger brother Yilu as duke of Dai commandery, and join Liu Xi with masses at Zhongshan.
translations.idiomatic: After Yiyi’s rescue of Sima Teng, Liu Kun had memorialized his brother Yilu as duke of Dai and combined forces with Liu Xi at Zhongshan.

sentences.zh: 王浚以琨侵己之地，數來擊琨，琨不能抗，由是聲實稍損。

translations.literal: Wang Jun because Kun encroached on his territory repeatedly came to strike Kun; Kun could not resist, whereby his name and substance gradually diminished.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jun attacked again and again over border disputes, and Liu Kun could not hold him off, so his prestige waned.

sentences.zh: 徐潤又譖令狐盛於琨曰：「盛將勸公稱帝矣。

translations.literal: Xu Run further slandered Linghu Sheng to Kun, saying, Sheng will urge you, lord, to declare yourself emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Run whispered that Linghu Sheng meant to push Liu Kun toward the throne.

sentences.zh: 」琨不之察，便殺之。

translations.literal: Kun did not examine it and then killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Without inquiry Liu Kun had Linghu Sheng executed.

sentences.zh: 琨母曰：「汝不能弘經略，駕豪傑，專欲除勝己以自安，當何以得濟！

translations.literal: Kun’s mother said, You cannot enlarge strategy and rein in heroes; you only wish to remove those better than yourself to feel safe—how will you ever succeed!
translations.idiomatic: His mother warned him: "You kill rivals instead of rallying heroes—you will never save Bing this way!

sentences.zh: 如是，禍必及我。

translations.literal: If it is so, disaster is sure to reach me.
translations.idiomatic: "If that is your course, ruin will find us all.

sentences.zh: 」不從。

translations.literal: He did not follow.
translations.idiomatic: He would not listen.

sentences.zh: 盛子泥奔于劉聰，具言虛實。

translations.literal: Sheng’s son Ni fled to Liu Cong and fully reported the true situation.
translations.idiomatic: Linghu Ni fled to Liu Cong and betrayed every weakness of Jinyang’s defense.

sentences.zh: 聰大喜，以泥爲鄉導。

translations.literal: Cong was greatly pleased and made Ni guide on the march.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Cong rejoiced and used Linghu Ni as his guide.

sentences.zh: 屬上黨太守襲醇降於聰，雁門烏丸復反，琨親率精兵出禦之。

translations.literal: It happened that the administrator of Shangdang, Xi Chun, surrendered to Cong, and the Yanmen Wuhuan rebelled again; Kun personally led crack troops out to meet them.
translations.idiomatic: When Shangdang surrendered and Yanmen Wuhuan rose, Liu Kun marched out in person with picked troops.

sentences.zh: 聰遣子粲及令狐泥乘虛襲晉陽，太原太守高喬以郡降聰，琨父母並遇害。

translations.literal: Cong sent son Can and Linghu Ni to exploit the emptiness and raid Jinyang; Taiyuan administrator Gao Qiao surrendered the commandery to Cong; Kun’s father and mother together met harm.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Cong sent Liu Can and Linghu Ni to strike Jinyang while Liu Kun was away; Taiyuan defected, and Liu Kun’s parents were killed.

sentences.zh: 琨引猗盧並力攻粲，大敗之，死者十五六。

translations.literal: Kun drew Yilu with combined strength to attack Can, greatly defeated him; dead were five or six tenths.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Kun and Yilu smashed Liu Can’s army, killing the larger part of his force.

sentences.zh: 琨乘勝追之，更不能克。

translations.literal: Kun rode victory to pursue him but could not overcome him further.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Kun pressed the pursuit but could not finish Liu Can.

sentences.zh: 猗盧以爲聰未可滅，遺琨牛羊車馬而去，留其將箕澹、段繁等戍晉陽。

translations.literal: Yilu thought Cong could not yet be extinguished, left Kun cattle, sheep, carts, and horses and departed, left his generals Ji Dan, Duan Fan, and others to garrison Jinyang.
translations.idiomatic: Yilu judged Liu Cong still too strong, gifted Liu Kun livestock and wagons, withdrew, and left Ji Dan and others to hold Jinyang.

sentences.zh: 琨志在復仇，而屈於力弱，泣血屍立，撫慰傷痍，移居陽邑城，以招集亡散。

translations.literal: Kun’s intent lay in revenge, yet he was bent by weakness of force; weeping blood he stood like a corpse, comforted the wounded, moved residence to Yangyi city to gather the scattered.
translations.idiomatic: Burning for vengeance but too weak to strike, he wept until he swayed, nursed the wounded, and moved to Yangyi to rally survivors.

sentences.zh: 湣帝即位，拜大將軍、都督并州諸軍事，加散騎常侍、假節。

translations.literal: When Emperor Min ascended the throne, he was appointed grand general, area commander-in-chief for military affairs of Bing province, added gentleman of the household for all purposes and credential staff.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Min named him grand general and military governor of Bing with staff and gentleman for all purposes.

sentences.zh: 琨上疏謝曰：

translations.literal: Kun submitted a memorial of thanks, saying:
translations.idiomatic: He presented a memorial of thanks—

sentences.zh: 陛下略臣大愆，錄臣小善，猥蒙天恩，光授殊寵，顯以蟬冕之榮，崇以上將之位。伏省詔書，五情飛越。

translations.literal: Your Majesty overlooks your subject’s great faults, records your subject’s small goodnesses, rashly confers Heaven’s grace, brightly grants extraordinary favor, showing with cicada-cap splendor the glory, honoring with the highest general’s rank. Bowing to read the edict, the five feelings soar and scatter.
translations.idiomatic: "You overlook my grave errors yet note my small services, shower me with honors and the cap of high office, and name me first general—reading your edict I tremble in every fiber.

sentences.zh: 臣聞晉文以郤縠爲元帥而定霸功，高祖以韓信爲大將而成王業，咸有敦詩閱禮之德，戎昭果毅之威，故能振豐功于荊南，拓洪基於河北。

translations.literal: Your subject has heard that Jin Wen made Xi Gu grand marshal and settled hegemonic merit, and the Supreme Ancestor made Han Xin grand general and completed kingly work; both had virtue of honoring the Odes and perusing the Rites and awesomeness of martial clarity, therefore they could shake great merit south of the Jing and widen great foundations north of the river.
translations.idiomatic: "Jin Wen and Han Gaozu built empires through men of both civil and martial genius—how dare a mediocrity like me claim their mantle?

sentences.zh: 況臣凡陋，擬蹤前哲，俯懼折鼎，慮在覆餗。昔曹沫三北，而收功于柯盟；馮異垂翅，而奮翼于澠池，皆能因敗爲成，以功補過。

translations.literal: Moreover your subject is mean and shallow, tracing tracks of former sages; bending fears the cauldron’s break, worry lies in overturning the stew. In antiquity Cao Mo thrice fled north yet gathered merit at the Ke covenant; Feng Yi hung wings yet flapped them at Mianchi; both could turn defeat into completion and mend fault with merit.
translations.idiomatic: "Yet Cao Mo and Feng Yi rose from failure—may I too mend my faults with deeds.

sentences.zh: 及麹允敗劉曜，斬趙冉，琨又表曰：

translations.literal: When Qu Yun defeated Liu Yao and beheaded Zhao Ran, Kun again submitted a memorial, saying:
translations.idiomatic: After Qu Yun’s victory over Liu Yao, Liu Kun sent another memorial:

sentences.zh: 逆胡劉聰，敢率犬羊，馮陵輦轂，人神發憤，遐邇奮怒。

translations.literal: The rebellious Hu Liu Cong dares to lead dogs and sheep, assail the imperial palanquin; men and spirits blaze with anger, near and far surge with rage.
translations.idiomatic: "Liu Cong’s barbarian hordes insult the throne; all the realm burns for revenge.

sentences.zh: 臣前表當與鮮卑猗盧克今年三月都會平陽，會匈羯石勒以三月三日徑掩薊城，大司馬、博陵公浚受其偽和，爲勒所虜，勒勢轉盛，欲來襲臣。

translations.literal: Your subject earlier memorialized that he should with the Xianbei Yilu this year in the third month jointly muster at Pingyang; it happened that the Xiongnu Jie Shi Le on the third day of the third month went straight to surprise Ji; the grand marshal, the Duke of Boling, Jun, accepted his false peace, was captured by Le; Le’s power turned ever greater and he wishes to come raid your subject.
translations.idiomatic: "I had planned to meet Yilu at Pingyang in the third month, but Shi Le struck Ji, took Wang Jun, and now threatens me.

sentences.zh: 城塢駭懼，志在自守。

translations.literal: Walled towns were terrified and their intent lay in self-defense.
translations.idiomatic: Every garrison froze in fear and dug in for self-defense.

sentences.zh: 又猗盧國內欲生奸謀，幸盧警慮，尋皆誅滅。

translations.literal: Moreover within Yilu’s state treacherous plots wished to arise; fortunately Yilu was alert and inquired, and soon all were executed and destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: Even Yilu’s own camp nearly mutinied until he purged the plotters.

sentences.zh: 遂使南北顧慮，用愆成舉，臣所以泣血宵吟，扼腕長歎者也。

translations.literal: Thereupon north and south looked to each other in worry, and the planned joint action was missed in time—this is why your subject weeps blood through the night and wrings his wrist in long sighs.
translations.idiomatic: North and south plans fell apart—hence my sleepless laments.

sentences.zh: 勒據襄國，與臣隔山，寇騎朝發，夕及臣城，同惡相求，其徒實繁。

translations.literal: Le occupies Xiangguo, separated from your subject by mountains; raiding cavalry set out at dawn and reach your subject’s city by evening; the wicked seek each other; their sort is truly many.
translations.idiomatic: "Shi Le holds Xiangguo a ridge away—his raiders can ride from dawn to my walls, and his allies multiply.

sentences.zh: 自東北八州，勒滅其七，先朝所授，存者唯臣。

translations.literal: From the eight northeast provinces Le has extinguished seven; what the former court invested survives only in your subject.
translations.idiomatic: "He has swallowed seven of the northeast’s eight provinces; I alone remain of the old commissions.

sentences.zh: 是以勒朝夕謀慮，以圖臣爲計，窺伺間隙，寇抄相尋，戎士不得解甲，百姓不得在野。

translations.literal: Therefore Le day and night plots and plans, taking plotting against your subject as his scheme, spying for gaps, raiding and copying in succession; armored soldiers cannot ungird, commoners cannot go to the wilds.
translations.idiomatic: "He schemes against me day and night; my men never shed armor and the people dare not leave the walls.

sentences.zh: 天網雖張，靈澤未及，唯臣孑然與寇爲伍。

translations.literal: Heaven’s net though spread, numinous grace has not reached; only your subject stands alone with the bandits as company.
translations.idiomatic: "Heaven’s justice tarries while I stand alone among wolves.

sentences.zh: 自守則稽聰之誅，進討則勒襲其後，進退唯-{谷}-，首尾狼狽。

translations.literal: To defend oneself then meets Cong’s punishment; to advance and punish then Le strikes from behind; advance and retreat are in the valley’s straits; head and tail are wolf and badger.
translations.idiomatic: "If I stay, Liu Cong crushes me; if I march, Shi Le stabs my rear—I am caught fore and aft.

sentences.zh: 徒懷憤踴，力不從願，慚怖征營，痛心疾首，形留所在，神馳寇庭。

translations.literal: In vain he harbors indignant leap; strength does not follow his wish; shame and terror course through him; he pains heart and splits head; form stays where he is while spirit gallops to the bandit court.
translations.idiomatic: "I burn with shame yet cannot strike; my body is here but my soul is already on the battlefield.

sentences.zh: 秋穀既登，胡馬已肥，前鋒諸軍並有至者，臣當首啟戎行，身先士卒。

translations.literal: Autumn grain having mounted, Hu horses are already fat; vanguard hosts all have arrived; your subject should first open the martial line and himself lead soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: "Autumn stores are in and barbarian horses fat; the vanguard is massing—I mean to lead from the front.

sentences.zh: 臣與二虜，勢不並立，聰、勒不梟，臣無歸志，庶憑陛下威靈，使微意獲展，然後隕首謝國，沒而無恨。

translations.literal: Your subject with the two foes cannot stand together; Cong and Le not beheaded, your subject has no mind to return; hoping to rely on Your Majesty’s awesome spirit, let a slight intent find display, then bow head and thank the state, dying without regret.
translations.idiomatic: "I cannot coexist with Liu Cong and Shi Le; grant me your majesty’s backing and I will spend my life repaying it, or fall without regret.

sentences.zh: 表文所陳，止於此處。

translations.literal: What the memorial sets forth stops at this point.
translations.idiomatic: So ends the memorial’s argument.

sentences.zh: 三年，帝遣兼大鴻臚趙廉持節拜琨爲司空、都督並冀幽三州諸軍事。

translations.literal: In the third year the Emperor sent concurrent grand herald Zhao Lian with staff to appoint Kun minister of works and area commander-in-chief for military affairs of Bing, Ji, and You provinces.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year the court sent Zhao Lian to name Liu Kun minister of works and governor of Bing, Ji, and You.

sentences.zh: 琨上表讓司空，受都督，克期與猗盧討劉聰。

translations.literal: Kun submitted a memorial declining minister of works, accepted the area command, and set a date with Yilu to punish Liu Cong.
translations.idiomatic: He declined the ministry but kept military command and fixed a date with Yilu against Liu Cong.

sentences.zh: 尋猗盧父子相圖，盧及兄子根皆病死，部落四散。

translations.literal: Soon Yilu father and son plotted against each other; Yilu and his elder brother’s son Gen both died of illness and the tribes scattered.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Yilu’s family feuded; he and his nephew Gen died and the tribes melted away.

sentences.zh: 琨子遵先質于盧，眾皆附之。

translations.literal: Kun’s son Zun earlier had been hostage with Lu; the masses all attached to him.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zun, long a hostage to Yilu, was acclaimed by the tribes.

sentences.zh: 及是，遵與箕澹等帥盧眾三萬人，馬牛羊十萬，悉來歸琨，琨由是復振，率數百騎自平城撫納之。

translations.literal: At this point Zun together with Ji Dan and others led Lu’s masses thirty thousand persons, horses, cattle, and sheep one hundred thousand, all to come submit to Kun; Kun thereby revived, leading several hundred horsemen from Pingcheng to soothe and accept them.
translations.idiomatic: Zun then led thirty thousand Xianbei and vast herds back to Liu Kun, who rode out from Pingcheng to welcome them and felt his strength return.

sentences.zh: 屬石勒攻樂平，太守韓據請救於琨，而琨自以士眾新合，欲因其銳以威勒。

translations.literal: It happened that Shi Le attacked Leping; Administrator Han Ju begged rescue from Kun, but Kun himself because his soldiers and masses were newly joined wished to use their keen edge to overawe Le.
translations.idiomatic: When Shi Le besieged Leping, Han Ju begged help; Liu Kun, trusting his newly swollen host, meant to overawe Shi Le.

sentences.zh: 箕澹諫曰：「此雖晉人，久在荒裔，未習恩信，難以法-{御}-。

translations.literal: Ji Dan remonstrated, saying, Though these are Jin people, long in wild borderlands they have not practiced grace and trust and are hard to rule by law.
translations.idiomatic: Ji Dan warned: "These troops are long out of Chinese discipline—law alone cannot harness them yet.

sentences.zh: 今內收鮮卑之餘穀，外抄殘胡之牛羊，且閉關守險，務農息士，既服化感義，然後用之，則功可立也。

translations.literal: Now within gather the Xianbei’s surplus grain, without raid the remnant Hu’s cattle and sheep, and for the while close passes and guard peril, work farming and rest the soldiers; once they have submitted to transformation and felt righteousness, then use them—then merit can be established.
translations.idiomatic: "Stockpile grain, raid stray herds, hold the passes, farm and rest until they truly accept us—then strike.

sentences.zh: 」琨不從，悉發其眾，命澹領步騎二萬爲前驅，琨自爲後繼。

translations.literal: Kun did not follow, sent out all his host, ordered Dan to lead twenty thousand foot and horse as vanguard, and Kun himself was rear support.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Kun ignored him, threw in every man, and sent Ji Dan ahead with twenty thousand while he followed.

sentences.zh: 勒先據險要，設伏以擊澹，大敗之，一軍皆沒，並土震駭。

translations.literal: Le first occupied the perilous passes, set ambushes to strike Dan, greatly defeated him; one army was entirely lost, and Bing soil quaked in terror.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Le seized the choke points, ambushed Ji Dan, annihilated his army, and shook Bing province.

sentences.zh: 尋又炎旱，琨窮蹙不能復守。

translations.literal: Soon again scorching drought; Kun was cornered and could not again defend.
translations.idiomatic: Drought followed; Liu Kun could no longer hold his ground.

sentences.zh: 幽州刺史鮮卑段匹磾數遣信要琨，欲與同獎王室。

translations.literal: Inspector of You province, the Xianbei Duan Pidi, several times sent letters inviting Kun, wishing together to aid the royal house.
translations.idiomatic: Duan Pidi of You, a Xianbei chief, urged Liu Kun to join him in restoring the Jin house.

sentences.zh: 琨由是率眾赴之，從飛狐人薊。

translations.literal: Kun thereupon led the masses to go to him, entering Ji through Flying Fox.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Kun marched to him through Flying Fox pass into Ji.

sentences.zh: 匹磾見之，甚相崇重，與琨結婚，約爲兄弟。

translations.literal: When Pidi saw him, he greatly honored him, married with Kun, and covenanted as brothers.
translations.idiomatic: Duan Pidi received him with honor, married into his family, and swore brotherhood.

sentences.zh: 是時西都不守，元帝稱制江左，琨乃令長史溫嶠勸進，於是河朔征鎮夷夏一百八十人連名上表，語在《元紀》。

translations.literal: At this time the western capital did not hold; the Prince of Langya exercised regency south of the river; Kun then ordered chief clerk Wen Qiao to urge advance; thereupon north-of-the-river zhen, garrison, Yi and Xia one hundred eighty persons jointly signed a memorial—the words are in the Basic Annals of Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: With Chang’an lost and Sima Rui regent in the south, Liu Kun had Wen Qiao draft the joint memorial of one hundred eighty northern commanders urging him to take the throne—the text stands in Rui’s annals.

sentences.zh: 令報曰：「豺狼肆毒，薦覆社稷，億兆顒顒，延首罔系。

translations.literal: The order replied, saying, Jackals and wolves unleash poison, repeatedly overturning the altars of soil and grain; hundred millions crane their necks, stretching heads with none to tie them.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Rui answered: "Savages have overturned the realm; the people crane their necks with no lord to bind them.

sentences.zh: 是以居於王位，以答天下，庶以克復聖主，掃蕩讎恥，豈可猥當隆極，此孤之至誠著於遐邇者也。

translations.literal: Therefore I dwell in the king’s position to answer the empire, hoping thereby to restore the sage lord and sweep away shame and hatred—how could I vulgarly mount the supreme step? This is this orphan’s utmost sincerity shown to far and near.
translations.idiomatic: "I hold the regency only to restore the emperor—not to seize the throne myself.

sentences.zh: 公受奕世之寵，極人臣之位，忠允義誠，精感天地。

translations.literal: The duke receives favor piled through generations, reaches the utmost of human minister rank, loyalty and trust, righteousness and sincerity, essence touching Heaven and earth.
translations.idiomatic: "You enjoy generations of grace and the highest ministerial rank; your loyalty moves heaven and earth.

sentences.zh: 實賴遠謀，共濟艱難。

translations.literal: Truly we rely on far plans to cross difficult peril together.
translations.idiomatic: "We depend on your long view to weather this storm.

sentences.zh: 南北迥邈，同契一致，萬里之外，心存咫尺。

translations.literal: South and north are vastly distant, yet share one tally and one intent; beyond ten thousand li, hearts remain a foot apart.
translations.idiomatic: "North and south are far apart yet of one mind; distance cannot sever us.

sentences.zh: 公其撫甯華戎，致罰丑類。

translations.literal: The duke shall soothe and quiet Hua and Rong and inflict punishment on the ugly classes.
translations.idiomatic: "Pacify Chinese and barbarian alike and punish the rebels.

sentences.zh: 動靜以聞。」

translations.literal: Movements and stillnesses shall be heard.
translations.idiomatic: "Keep me informed of every move.

sentences.zh: 琨與匹磾期討石勒，匹磾推琨爲大都督，歃血載書，檄諸方守，俱集襄國。

translations.literal: Kun with Pidi set a date to punish Shi Le; Pidi pushed Kun as grand commander-in-chief, smeared blood and carried the covenant text, summoned the various garrison defenders, all to gather at Xiangguo.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Kun and Duan Pidi swore a blood oath at Xiangguo, named Liu Kun supreme commander, and called every garrison to join them against Shi Le.

sentences.zh: 琨、匹磾進屯固安，以俟眾軍。

translations.literal: Kun and Pidi advanced and encamped at Gu'an to await the mass of armies.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Kun and Duan Pidi moved forward and camped at Gu'an to wait for the allied forces.

sentences.zh: 匹磾從弟末波納勒厚賂，獨不進，乃沮其計。

translations.literal: Pidi's cousin Mobo accepted lavish bribes from Shi Le, alone did not advance, and thereby disrupted their plan.
translations.idiomatic: Duan Pidi's cousin Duan Mobo had taken heavy bribes from Shi Le; he alone held back, and the operation fell through.

sentences.zh: 琨、匹磾以勢弱而退。

translations.literal: Kun and Pidi withdrew because their strength was weak.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Kun and Duan Pidi pulled back because their position was too weak.

sentences.zh: 是歳，元帝轉琨爲侍中、太尉，其餘如故，並贈名刀。

translations.literal: That year Emperor Yuan transferred Kun to Palace Attendant and Grand Commandant; the rest remained as before, and a famous sword was also bestowed.
translations.idiomatic: That year Emperor Yuan moved Liu Kun to Palace Attendant and Grand Commandant, left his other appointments unchanged, and presented him with a celebrated blade as well.

sentences.zh: 琨答曰：「謹當躬自執佩，馘截二虜。」

translations.literal: Kun replied, "I shall respectfully wear it on my person myself and cut off the heads of the two enemy bands.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Kun answered, "I will wear it at my belt in person and strike down the two rebel hosts.

sentences.zh: 匹磾奔其兄喪，琨遣世子群送之，而末波率眾要擊匹磾而敗走之，群爲末波所得。

translations.literal: Pidi went to mourn his elder brother; Kun sent heir son Qun to escort him, but Mobo led forces to intercept Pidi and routed him; Qun was captured by Mobo.
translations.idiomatic: When Duan Pidi went to attend his brother's funeral, Liu Kun sent his heir apparent Liu Qun to see him off; Duan Mobo then ambushed Duan Pidi with troops and drove him off, and Liu Qun fell into Mobo's hands.

sentences.zh: 末波厚禮之，許以琨爲幽州刺史，共結盟而襲匹磾，密遣使齎群書請琨爲內應，而爲匹磾邏騎所得。

translations.literal: Mobo treated him generously, promised to make Kun Inspector of Youzhou, allied to strike Pidi, secretly sent an envoy bearing Qun's letter asking Kun to be inner responder, but it was obtained by Pidi's patrol riders.
translations.idiomatic: Mobo honored Liu Qun lavishly and promised to install Liu Kun as inspector of Youzhou; they swore alliance and planned to attack Duan Pidi. A secret messenger carried Liu Qun's letter urging Liu Kun to act from within—but Duan Pidi's scouts intercepted it.

sentences.zh: 時琨別屯故征北府小城，不之知也。

translations.literal: At the time Kun was separately encamped at the small fort of the former headquarters of the general who conquered the north and did not know of it.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Kun was camped apart at the minor fort of the old northern expedition headquarters and knew nothing of this.

sentences.zh: 因來見匹磾，匹磾以群書示琨曰：「意亦不疑公，是以白公耳。

translations.literal: Therefore he came to see Pidi; Pidi showed Kun Qun's letter and said, "In my heart I also do not doubt you; therefore I inform you.
translations.idiomatic: So Liu Kun came to see Duan Pidi, who showed him Liu Qun's letter and said, "I never doubted you in intent; I am only telling you openly.

sentences.zh: 」琨曰：「與公同盟，志獎王室，仰憑威力，庶雪國家之恥。

translations.literal: Kun said, "With you I swore alliance, intent on aiding the royal house; relying on your might I hoped to wipe away the state's shame.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Kun replied, "We joined you in alliance to sustain the house of Jin; I looked to your strength in the hope of avenging the nation's humiliation.

sentences.zh: 若兒書密達，亦終不以一子之故負公忘義也。

translations.literal: If my son's letter had reached me secretly, still I would not for one child's sake betray you and forget righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: Even if my son's letter had reached me in secret, I would never have sacrificed my duty to you for the sake of one child.

sentences.zh: 」匹磾雅重琨，初無害琨志，將聽還屯。

translations.literal: Pidi greatly esteemed Kun and at first had no intent to harm Kun; he was about to allow him to return to camp.
translations.idiomatic: Duan Pidi respected Liu Kun deeply and had meant him no harm at first; he was ready to let him go back to his camp.

sentences.zh: 其中弟叔軍好學有智謀，爲匹磾所信，謂匹磾曰：「吾胡夷耳，所以能服晉人者，畏吾眾也。

translations.literal: His middle younger brother Shujun loved learning and had stratagems, was trusted by Pidi, and said to Pidi, "We are Hu barbarians; the reason we can subdue Jin people is that they fear our multitude.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Shujun was learned and shrewd and enjoyed Duan Pidi's confidence. He told Duan Pidi, "We are barbarians; the Jin submit to us only because they fear our numbers.

sentences.zh: 今我骨肉構禍，是其良圖之日，若有奉琨以起，吾族盡矣。

translations.literal: Now our flesh and bone raise calamity among themselves—this is their day for a good plan; if anyone rallies Kun to rise, our clan will be wiped out.
translations.idiomatic: Now our own kin are tearing one another apart—their opening has come. If anyone raises Liu Kun against us, our whole line is finished.

sentences.zh: 」匹磾遂留琨。

translations.literal: Pidi therefore detained Kun.
translations.idiomatic: Duan Pidi then kept Liu Kun in custody.

sentences.zh: 琨之庶長子遵懼誅，與琨左長史楊橋、并州治中如綏閉門自守。

translations.literal: Kun's eldest son by a concubine, Zun, feared execution; together with Kun's senior clerk of the left Yang Qiao and Bingzhou aide Ru Sui he barred the gates and defended.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Kun's eldest son by a concubine, Liu Zun, feared execution; with Liu Kun's senior clerk of the left Yang Qiao and Bingzhou headquarters aide Ru Sui he shut the gates and held the compound.

sentences.zh: 匹磾諭之不得，因縱兵攻之。

translations.literal: Pidi could not persuade them and therefore unleashed troops to attack them.
translations.idiomatic: Duan Pidi could not talk them down and sent troops to storm the position.

sentences.zh: 琨將龍季猛迫於乏食，遂斬橋、綏而降。

translations.literal: Kun's officer Long Jimeng, pressed by lack of food, then slew Yang Qiao and Ru Sui and surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Kun's general Long Jimeng, starving for supplies, cut down Yang Qiao and Ru Sui and capitulated.

sentences.zh: 初，琨之去晉陽也，慮及危亡而大恥不雪，亦知夷狄難以義伏，冀輸寫至誠，僥倖萬一。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Kun left Jinyang, he reckoned with peril and ruin while the great shame went unavenged; he also knew barbarians are hard to subdue with righteousness, yet hoped to pour out utmost sincerity and seek one chance in ten thousand.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Kun had left Jinyang he knew he faced ruin while the great shame of defeat went unavenged; he understood too that nomads could not be bound by moral appeals alone, yet he hoped candor might win an unlikely opening.

sentences.zh: 每見將佐，發言慷慨，悲其道窮，欲率部曲列於賊壘。

translations.literal: Whenever he saw commanders and aides he spoke forthrightly and with grief that his path was exhausted, wishing to lead his household troops and draw up before the enemy ramparts.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he met his officers he spoke with fierce clarity, grieving that his options had run out and wishing to march his retainers straight to the enemy lines.

sentences.zh: 斯謀未果，竟爲匹磾所拘。

translations.literal: That plan did not succeed; in the end he was detained by Pidi.
translations.idiomatic: The plan never came off; he ended in Duan Pidi's custody.

sentences.zh: 自知必死，神色怡如也。

translations.literal: Knowing he must die, his expression was serene.
translations.idiomatic: Certain he would die, he remained composed in face and bearing.

sentences.zh: 爲五言詩贈其別駕盧諶曰：

translations.literal: He made a pentasyllabic poem to present to his aide Lu Chen, saying:
translations.idiomatic: He addressed a pentasyllabic poem to his administrative aide Lu Chen:

translations.literal: The source line consists of a colon introducing the verses below.
translations.idiomatic: A colon in the edition introduces the poem that follows.

sentences.zh: 琨詩託意非常，攄暢幽憤，遠想張陳，感鴻門、白登之事，用以激諶。

translations.literal: Kun's poem entrusted meaning beyond the ordinary, poured forth hidden resentment, thought far of Zhang and Chen, was moved by Hongmen and Baideng affairs, using them to rouse Chen.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Kun's poem spoke with unusual intensity, venting buried grievance; echoing Zhang Liang and Chen Ping and the crises at Hongmen and Baideng, he meant to galvanize Lu Chen.

sentences.zh: 諶素無奇略，以常詞酬和，殊乖琨心，重以詩贈之，乃謂琨曰：「前篇帝王大志，非人臣所言矣。」

translations.literal: Chen had never had remarkable strategies; he replied in harmony with ordinary phrases, greatly contrary to Kun's mind; Kun again presented him with a poem, whereupon he said to Kun, "The former piece speaks the great ambition of an emperor—it is not what a subject should say.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Chen had never been a strategist; he answered in bland verse that missed Liu Kun's intent entirely. When Liu Kun sent another poem, Lu told him, "Your previous poem voiced an emperor's ambitions—it is not language fit for a minister.

sentences.zh: 然琨既忠於晉室，素有重望，被拘經月，遠近憤歎。

translations.literal: Yet Kun was loyal to the Jin house and long held heavy esteem; detained for months, near and far were indignant and sighed.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Liu Kun's loyalty to Jin and his long-standing prestige meant that when he languished under arrest for months, people everywhere seethed with anger and sorrow.

sentences.zh: 匹磾所署代郡太守辟閭嵩，與琨所署雁門太守王據、後將軍韓據連謀，密作攻具，欲以襲匹磾。

translations.literal: Pilü Song, whom Pidi had appointed governor of Dai commandery, conspired with Wang Ju and Han Ju—governor of Yanmen and general of the rear whom Kun had appointed—secretly making assault equipment intending thereby to strike Pidi.
translations.idiomatic: Pilü Song, whom Duan Pidi had installed as governor of Dai, joined Wang Ju and Han Ju—the governor of Yanmen and general of the rear whom Liu Kun had appointed—in a plot. They forged siege gear in secret to attack Duan Pidi.

sentences.zh: 而韓據女爲匹磾兒妾，聞其謀而告之匹磾，於是執王據、辟閭嵩及其徒黨悉誅之。

translations.literal: But Han Ju's daughter was Pidi's son's concubine; she heard their plot and informed Pidi; thereupon he seized Wang Ju, Pilü Song, and their entire faction and executed them all.
translations.idiomatic: Han Ju's daughter was a concubine of Duan Pidi's son; she overheard the scheme and told Duan Pidi, who arrested Wang Ju and Pilü Song and put their whole party to death.

sentences.zh: 會王敦密使匹磾殺琨，匹磾又懼眾反己，遂稱有詔收琨。

translations.literal: It happened that Wang Dun secretly instructed Pidi to kill Kun; Pidi also feared the multitude would turn against him, therefore claimed there was an edict to seize Kun.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dun had secretly ordered Duan Pidi to kill Liu Kun; Duan Pidi also feared his men might rebel, so he claimed an imperial warrant to arrest Liu Kun.

sentences.zh: 初，琨聞敦使到，謂其子曰：「處仲使來而不我告，是殺我也。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Kun heard Dun's envoy had arrived, he told his son, "Zhong's envoy comes and does not inform me—this is to kill me.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, upon hearing Wang Dun's messenger had come, Liu Kun said to his son, "If Zhong sends an envoy and keeps me in the dark, he means to kill me.

sentences.zh: 死生有命，但恨仇恥不雪，無以下見二親耳。

translations.literal: Death and life have fate; only I regret enemy shame is not avenged—I have no way to meet my two parents below.
translations.idiomatic: Life and death are Heaven's—but I hate that I cannot wash away our shame and have no face to meet my parents in the grave.

sentences.zh: 」因歔欷不能自勝。

translations.literal: Thereupon he sobbed and could not master himself.
translations.idiomatic: He broke into tears he could not hold back.

sentences.zh: 匹磾遂縊之，時年四十八。

translations.literal: Pidi then strangled him; at the time he was forty-eight.
translations.idiomatic: Duan Pidi strangled him; Liu Kun was forty-eight.

sentences.zh: 子侄四人俱被害。

translations.literal: Four sons and nephews were all killed.
translations.idiomatic: Four of his sons and nephews died with him.

sentences.zh: 朝廷以匹磾尚強，當爲國討石勒，不舉琨哀。

translations.literal: The court, because Pidi was still strong and ought for the state to attack Shi Le, did not raise mourning for Kun.
translations.idiomatic: The court, judging Duan Pidi still useful against Shi Le for the realm, declined to observe mourning for Liu Kun.

sentences.zh: 三年，琨故從事中郎盧諶、崔悅等上表理琨曰：

translations.literal: In the third year, Kun's former administrative aides Lu Chen and Cui Yue and others submitted a memorial vindicating Kun, saying:
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of the reign, Liu Kun's former administrative aides Lu Chen and Cui Yue memorialized to clear his name:

sentences.zh: :{{blue|　　臣聞經國之體，在於崇明典刑；

translations.literal: "Your servants have heard that the substance of ordering the state lies in clarifying and elevating statutes and models;
translations.idiomatic: "We your ministers have learned that the foundation of ruling the realm rests on holding up law and precedent as the standard;

sentences.zh: 立政之務，在於固慎關塞。

translations.literal: the tasks of establishing government lie in securing and cautiously guarding passes and frontiers.
translations.idiomatic: the business of government lies in sealing and guarding the borders with care.

sentences.zh: 況方嶽之臣，殺生之柄，而可不正其枉直，以杜其奸邪哉！

translations.literal: How much more for ministers who are regional pillars, holding the power of life and death—how can one fail to straighten what is crooked or upright and thereby block treachery!
translations.idiomatic: How much more must regional ministers who hold the power of life and death judge crooked and straight without error and shut the door to villainy!

sentences.zh: 竊見故司空、廣武侯琨，在惠帝擾攘之際，值群後鼎沸之難，戮力皇家，義誠彌厲，躬統華夷，親受矢石，石超授首，呂朗面縛，社稷克寧，鑾輿反駕，奉迎之勳，琨實爲隆，此琨效忠之一驗也。

translations.literal: We privately observe the former Minister of Works and Marquis of Guangwu, Kun: amid Emperor Hui's turmoil he encountered the cauldron-boiling hardship of the assembled lords; he exerted strength for the imperial house, his devotion burned ever brighter; he personally commanded Chinese and barbarians, personally endured arrows and stones; Shi Chao was beheaded, Lü Lang bound face-down; the altars of soil and grain were secured and the imperial carriage returned—among merits of welcome Kun's was the greatest: this is one proof of Kun's loyal service.
translations.idiomatic: Consider the late minister of works and marquis of Guangwu, Liu Kun: when Emperor Hui's reign dissolved into chaos and rival princes tore the realm apart, he strained every nerve for the throne; his zeal mounted as he led Hu and Han alike under hostile fire—Shi Chao lost his head and Lü Lang was bound; the dynasty steadied and the imperial carriage returned. Among those who helped restore the court, none surpassed Liu Kun; here is one plain witness to his loyalty.

sentences.zh: 其後并州刺史、東贏公騰以晉川荒匱，移鎮臨漳，太原、西河盡徙三魏。

translations.literal: Afterward Bingzhou inspector Prince Dongying Teng, because the Jin heartland was barren and depleted, shifted his garrison to Linzhang; Taiyuan and Xihe were wholly relocated into the three Wei regions.
translations.idiomatic: Later the Bingzhou inspector and Prince of Dongying, Sima Teng, finding the central plains exhausted of grain, moved his headquarters to Linzhang and evacuated Taiyuan and Xihe into the three Wei commanderies.

sentences.zh: 琨受任并州，屬承其弊，到官之日，遺戸無幾，當易危之勢，處難濟之土，鳩集傷痍，撫和戎狄，數年之間，公私漸振。

translations.literal: Kun received assignment to Bingzhou, inheriting its ruin; the day he arrived at office remaining households were few; facing easy peril's posture, occupying hard-to-aid territory, he gathered the wounded and ruined, soothed and reconciled Rong and Di; within several years public and private gradually revived.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Kun took Bingzhou in that wreckage: when he entered office almost no people remained. He stood where collapse was easiest on ground hardest to salvage—yet he gathered the shattered, pacified the tribes, and within a few years public stores and private livelihoods began to revive.

sentences.zh: 會京都失守，群逆縱逸，邊萌頓僕，苟懷宴安，咸以爲并州之地四塞爲困，且可閉關守險，畜資養徒，抗辭厲聲，忠亮奮發，以爲天子沈辱而不隕身死節，情非所安，遂乃跋履山川，東西征討。

translations.literal: When the capital fell and rebel bands ran rampant, border sprouts collapsed prostrate; had they hugged ease and comfort, all would have thought Bingzhou's land boxed by four barriers could close passes and guard narrows, hoard goods and nurture followers—but with defiant words and stern voice, loyalty and brightness surged forth; Kun held that while the Son of Heaven sank in humiliation, not to risk body and die for principle was not where feeling could rest; therefore he traversed mountains and rivers campaigning east and west.
translations.idiomatic: When Luoyang fell and rebels ran free, the frontier populace lay in ruins. An easier course would have been to seal Bingzhou's mountain barriers, hoard supplies, and wait—but Liu Kun refused ease while the emperor suffered shame; loyalty blazed in him, and he marched back and forth across the north to fight east and west.

sentences.zh: 屠各乘虛，晉陽沮潰，琨父母罹屠戮之殃，門族受殲夷之禍。

translations.literal: The Tuge seized the void; Jinyang broke and collapsed; Kun's parents suffered slaughter's calamity and his clan met annihilation's disaster.
translations.idiomatic: The Tuge struck while the defense was hollow; Jinyang collapsed. Liu Kun's parents were butchered and his entire clan swept away.

sentences.zh: 向使琨從州人之心，爲自守之計，則聖朝未必加誅，而族黨可以不喪。

translations.literal: Had Kun followed the hearts of his provincial people and made plans only for self-defense, then the sagely court might not necessarily have punished him, and clan and kin might have avoided destruction.
translations.idiomatic: Had Liu Kun listened to local opinion and dug in only for self-defense, the court might never have faulted him and his kin might have survived.

sentences.zh: 及猗盧敗亂，晉人歸奔，琨于平城納其初附。

translations.literal: When Yilu was defeated in turmoil, Jin people fled homeward; Kun at Pingcheng accepted their first adherence.
translations.idiomatic: When Tuoba Yilu's host unraveled, displaced Jin subjects streamed back; Liu Kun took them in at Pingcheng when they first rallied to him.

sentences.zh: 將軍箕澹又以爲此雖晉人，久在荒裔，難以法整，不可便用。

translations.literal: General Ji Dan also held that although these were Jin people, long in remote borderlands, they were hard to regulate by law and could not be employed forthwith.
translations.idiomatic: General Ji Dan argued that although they were ethnically Jin, years on the frontier had left them beyond quick discipline—they could not be thrown straight into the ranks.

sentences.zh: 琨又讓之，義形於色。

translations.literal: Kun again remonstrated with him; righteousness showed in his expression.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Kun reproached him again; moral conviction showed plain on his face.

sentences.zh: 假從澹議，偷于苟存，則晏然於並土，必不亡身于燕薊也。

translations.literal: Had he followed Dan's counsel and stolen mere survival, then peacefully on Bing soil he would surely not have lost his life in Yan and Ji.
translations.idiomatic: Had he yielded to Ji Dan and chosen bare survival, he could have stayed safely on Bingzhou soil and would never have died in the Yan–Ji region.

sentences.zh: 琨自以備位方嶽，綱維不舉，無緣虛荷大任，坐居三司，是以陛下登阼，使引衍告遜，前後章表，具陳誠款。

translations.literal: Kun himself considered that occupying regional pillar's position yet nets not raised had no cause vainly to shoulder great commission and sit occupying three dukes; therefore when Your Majesty ascended the throne he caused Yin to be cited to declare yielding—before and after memorials fully declared sincere earnestness.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Kun knew he held a governor's post yet failed to impose order; he had no wish to bear grand titles empty-handed. When Your Majesty took the throne he cited precedent and offered to step aside—memorial after memorial laid his sincerity bare.

sentences.zh: 尋令從事中郎臣續澹以章綬節傳奉還本朝，與匹磾使榮邵期一時俱發。

translations.literal: Shortly he ordered administrative aide Xu Dan to return seals, ribbons, tally, and relay credential to the court, together with Pidi's envoy Rong Shao timed to depart together.
translations.idiomatic: He soon ordered his administrative aide Xu Dan to send the seals, ribbons, tally, and courier credentials back to court at the same hour as Duan Pidi's envoy Rong Shao departed.

sentences.zh: 又匹磾以琨王室大臣，懼奪己威重，忌琨之形，漸彰於外。

translations.literal: Moreover Pidi, because Kun was a great minister of the royal house, feared Kun would seize his authority and weight; the pattern of jealousy toward Kun gradually showed outward.
translations.idiomatic: Duan Pidi saw Liu Kun as a pillar of the dynasty and feared losing stature to him; his mistrust soon showed for all to see.

sentences.zh: 琨知其如此，慮不可久，欲遣妻息大小盡詣京城，以其門室一委陛下。

translations.literal: Kun knew it was thus, feared it could not last long, wished to send wives and children great and small all to the capital city, entrusting his household wholesale to Your Majesty.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing this, Liu Kun knew he could not endure long in place and wished to send every wife and child to the capital and leave his household entirely in Your Majesty's hands.

sentences.zh: 有征舉之會，則身充一卒；

translations.literal: If there were occasions for levy and muster, then his person would serve as one soldier;
translations.idiomatic: Whenever war called, he would enlist as a common soldier;

sentences.zh: 若匹磾縱凶慝，則妻息可免。

translations.literal: if Pidi indulged fierce wickedness, then wives and children could be spared.
translations.idiomatic: should Duan Pidi turn vicious, at least his family would be beyond reach.

sentences.zh: 具令臣澹密宣此旨，求詔敕路次，令相迎衞。

translations.literal: He fully ordered minister Dan secretly to proclaim this intent, seeking edict instruction along the route ordering mutual welcome and guard.
translations.idiomatic: He instructed Xu Dan in secret to relay this and asked for an edict ordering escorts along the road to receive them.

sentences.zh: 會王成從平陽逃來，説南陽王保稱號隴右，士眾甚盛，當移關中。

translations.literal: It happened that Wang Cheng fled from Pingyang and reported Prince Nanyang Bao had proclaimed a title in Longyou right with very numerous soldiers and ought to shift into Guanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: Then Wang Cheng escaped from Pingyang with word that Prince of Nanyang Sima Bao had styled himself west of Long with a large army and meant to move into Guanzhong.

sentences.zh: 匹磾聞此，私懷顧望，留停榮邵，欲遣前兼鴻臚邊邈奉使詣保，懼澹獨南，言其此事，遂不許引路。

translations.literal: Pidi heard this and privately harbored hesitation; he detained Rong Shao and wished to send former concurrent grand herald Bian Miao as envoy to Bao; fearing Dan alone going south would speak of this matter, he therefore did not permit opening the route.
translations.idiomatic: Duan Pidi hesitated: he held Rong Shao back and meant to send the former vice minister Bian Miao to Sima Bao—yet feared Xu Dan would reach the south alone and expose the plan, so he refused safe-conduct.

sentences.zh: 丹誠赤心，卒不上達。

translations.literal: Cinnabar sincerity and red heart in the end did not ascend and reach.
translations.idiomatic: His loyal heart never reached the throne.

sentences.zh: 匹磾兄眷喪亡，嗣子幼弱，欲因奔喪奪取其國。

translations.literal: Pidi's elder brother Juan died; the heir son was young and weak; Pidi wished by means of mourning rush to seize his state.
translations.idiomatic: When Duan Pidi's brother Duan Juan died leaving a young heir, Duan Pidi meant to exploit the funeral and seize his domain.

sentences.zh: 又自以欺國陵家，懷邪樂禍，恐父母宗黨不容其罪，是以卷甲櫜弓，陰圖作亂，欲害其從叔驎、從弟末波等，以取其國。

translations.literal: Moreover he himself deceived state and mistreated family, harbored wickedness and rejoiced in calamity, feared parents and clan kin would not tolerate his crimes; therefore he rolled up armor and bagged bows, secretly plotted rebellion, wished to harm his cousin uncles Lin and cousin younger brothers Mobo and others to seize their state.
translations.idiomatic: He had wronged the court and his kin, relished intrigue and disaster, and feared his clan would not forgive him—so he packed arms and plotted in secret to murder cousins such as Duan Lin and Duan Mobo and seize their lands.

sentences.zh: 匹磾親信密告驎、波，驎、波乃遣人距之，匹磾僅以身免。

translations.literal: Pidi's trusted men secretly informed Lin and Bo; Lin and Bo then sent men to resist him; Pidi barely escaped with his body alone.
translations.idiomatic: Duan Pidi's confidants tipped off Duan Lin and Mobo, who blocked him—Duan Pidi barely escaped alive.

sentences.zh: 百姓謂匹磾已沒，皆憑向琨。

translations.literal: The hundred surnames thought Pidi had already perished; all leaned toward Kun.
translations.idiomatic: The people assumed Duan Pidi was dead and turned to Liu Kun for leadership.

sentences.zh: 若琨于時有害匹磾之情，則居然可擒，不復營於人力。

translations.literal: If Kun at that time had intention to harm Pidi, then plainly he could have been seized without further laboring human effort.
translations.idiomatic: Had Liu Kun meant to destroy Duan Pidi then, he could have taken him with ease—no elaborate maneuver would have been needed.

sentences.zh: 自此之後，上下並離，匹磾遂欲盡勒胡晉，徙居上-{谷}-。

translations.literal: From this after, superiors and inferiors together separated; Pidi then wished fully to force Hu and Jin and relocate to dwell in Shang-{gu}-.
translations.idiomatic: After that, ruler and followers split; Duan Pidi meant to drive every Hu and Han follower into Shang-{gu}- commandery.

sentences.zh: 琨深不然之，勸移厭次，南憑朝廷。

translations.literal: Kun deeply rejected this, urged moving to Yanqi, relying south on the court.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Kun opposed this fiercely and urged shifting to Yanqi to keep the south anchored to the court.

sentences.zh: 匹磾不能納，反禍害父息四人，從兄二息同時並命。

translations.literal: Pidi could not accept; contrarywise he harmed and killed four fathers and sons, two sons of elder cousins at the same time losing lives together.
translations.idiomatic: Duan Pidi would not listen and struck at Liu Kun's house—four sons or sons and fathers fell together with two nephews by Liu Kun's cousins in the same slaughter.

sentences.zh: 琨未遇害，知匹磾必有禍心，語臣等云：「受國厚恩，不能克報，雖才略不及，亦由遇此厄運。

translations.literal: Before Kun met harm, he knew Pidi must harbor harmful intent; he told your servants and others saying, "Receiving the state's thick grace I could not repay it fully; although talent and strategy did not reach, it is also because I encountered this ill fate.
translations.idiomatic: Before he died Liu Kun knew Duan Pidi meant him ill. He told us, "The state favored me beyond my deserts and I repaid it poorly—partly from limited ability, partly from cruel fortune.

sentences.zh: 人誰不死，死生命也。

translations.literal: Among men who does not die—death and life are fate's decree.
translations.idiomatic: All men die; life and death are Heaven's sentence.

sentences.zh: 唯恨下不能效節于一方，上不得歸誠于陛下。

translations.literal: Only I regret below I could not display fidelity in one region, above I could not return sincerity to Your Majesty.
translations.idiomatic: I only regret I could not prove loyal on my frontier or lay my heart before Your Majesty.

sentences.zh: 」辭旨慷慨，動於左右。

translations.literal: The wording's intent was stirring; it moved those left and right.
translations.idiomatic: His words thrilled and moved everyone present.

sentences.zh: 匹磾既害琨，橫加誣謗，言琨欲窺神器，謀圖不軌。

translations.literal: After Pidi harmed Kun, he recklessly added slander, saying Kun wished to spy on the divine vessel and plot transgression.
translations.idiomatic: After murdering Liu Kun, Duan Pidi slandered him wildly—claiming he coveted the throne and plotted rebellion.

sentences.zh: 琨免述囂頑凶之思，又無信布懼誅之情，崎嶇亂亡之際，夾肩異類之間，而有如此之心哉！

translations.literal: Kun lacked the thinking of stubborn villainy like Shu Ao, also lacked the emotion of Xin and Bu fearing execution—amid jagged chaos and ruin's moment, sandwiched between alien kinds—yet could have such a heart!
translations.idiomatic: Liu Kun was no Wei Ao nursing treason in the hills, nor Han Xin nor Ying Bu dreading the headsman's axe—hemmed by chaos and alien armies, how could he dream of usurping the mandate!

sentences.zh: 雖臧獲之愚，廝養之智，猶不爲之，況在國士之列，忠節先著者乎！

translations.literal: Even slaves' stupidity and pages' wit still would not do this—how much more one in the ranks of state gentlemen whose loyalty and fidelity showed first!
translations.idiomatic: The meanest slave would shrink from such a plot—let alone a man honored as a pillar of the state whose loyalty was already proven!

translations.idiomatic: End of the first section of the memorial.

sentences.zh: :{{blue|　　匹磾之害琨，稱陛下密詔。

translations.literal: As to Pidi's harming Kun, he claimed Your Majesty's secret edict.
translations.idiomatic: When Duan Pidi murdered Liu Kun, he claimed a secret order from Your Majesty.

sentences.zh: 琨信有罪，陛下加誅，自當肆諸市朝，與眾棄之，不令殊俗之豎戮臺輔之臣，亦已明矣。

translations.literal: If Kun truly had guilt and Your Majesty added execution, naturally he should be exposed in market and court and abandoned with the multitude—not allowing alien customs' striplings to slaughter pillar ministers of the terrace—this too is already clear.
translations.idiomatic: If Liu Kun were guilty, Your Majesty would execute him in the public square for all to see—you would never leave a frontier upstart to butcher a chief minister of state; that much is plain.

sentences.zh: 然則擅詔有罪，雖小必誅；

translations.literal: Thus then usurping edict has guilt—though small must be punished;
translations.idiomatic: Usurping an imperial command is a crime—small as it may be, it must be punished;

sentences.zh: 矯制有功，雖大不論，正以興替之根咸在於此，開塞之由不可不閉故也。

translations.literal: forging commission having merit—though great is not discussed—the reason rise and fall's roots all lie herein, open and block's causes cannot fail to be closed is why.
translations.idiomatic: while forging orders for gain, however great, goes unpunished—precisely because dynastic survival turns on this principle, and the floodgates of abuse must stay shut.

sentences.zh: 而匹磾無所顧忌，怙亂專殺，虛假王命，虐害鼎臣，辱諸夏之望，敗王室之法，是可忍也，孰不可忍！

translations.literal: Yet Pidi had nothing he regarded as taboo, relied on turmoil to kill by sole authority, falsely borrowed kingly command, cruelly harmed tripod ministers, insulted the Zhongxia's expectations, defeated royal house's law—if this may be endured, what cannot be endured!
translations.idiomatic: Yet Duan Pidi respects no limits: he thrives on chaos, kills at will, counterfeits royal orders, tortures chief ministers, humiliates the hopes of the civilized regions, and tramples the laws of the throne—if that may be borne, what cannot!

sentences.zh: 若聖朝猶加隱忍，未明大體，則不逞之人襲匹磾之跡，殺生自由，好惡任意，陛下將何以誅之哉！

translations.literal: If the sagely court still adds hidden forbearance, not clarifying great substance, then unrestrained persons will copy Pidi's tracks—life and killing free, love and hate following whim—how will Your Majesty punish them!
translations.idiomatic: If the court still shrinks from acting and misses the larger issue, every adventurer will imitate Duan Pidi—killing at pleasure, rewarding or ruining on a whim—and how then will Your Majesty hold anyone to account!

sentences.zh: 折沖厭難，唯存戰勝之將；

translations.literal: Repelling assault and suppressing hardship—only surviving are victory-winning generals;
translations.idiomatic: To blunt enemy blows and end crises you look to generals who actually win;

sentences.zh: 除暴討亂，必須知略之臣。

translations.literal: eliminating violence and punishing turmoil—must have ministers of knowledge and strategy.
translations.idiomatic: to purge cruelty and rebellion you need ministers of judgment and strategy.

sentences.zh: 故古語云「山有猛獸，藜藿爲之不采」，非虛言矣。

translations.literal: Therefore an ancient saying states, "When mountains have fierce beasts, pigweed and bean-leaves on its account are not gathered"—it is not empty speech.
translations.idiomatic: The proverb says, "Where a mountain holds fierce beasts, even wild greens go unpicked"—and that is no idle phrase.

sentences.zh: 自河以北，幽-{并}-以南，醜類有所顧憚者，唯琨而已。

translations.literal: From north of the river to south of You-{Bing}-, among ugly sorts those whom something causes to fear and dread—only Kun alone.
translations.idiomatic: North of the Yellow River and south of You-{Bing}-, among hostile bands the only man they still feared was Liu Kun.

sentences.zh: 琨受害之後，羣凶欣欣，莫不得意，鼓行中州，曾無纖介，此又華夷小大所以長歎者也。

translations.literal: After Kun suffered harm, the crowd of villains rejoiced greatly, none not obtaining their desire; they beat drums marching through the central plain—never was there the slightest obstruction—this again is why Chinese and barbarians great and small sigh long.
translations.idiomatic: Once Liu Kun fell, every villain rejoiced; they marched unchecked through the Central Plain while Chinese and barbarians alike groaned—another reason for endless lament.

translations.idiomatic: End of the second section of the memorial.

sentences.zh: :{{blue|　　伏惟陛下睿聖之隆，中興之緒，方將平章典刑，以經序萬國。

translations.literal: We humbly consider Your Majesty's sagely holiness's elevation, restoration's continuation—about to equalize and clarify statutes and models to regulate and order myriad states.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty's sagely brilliance lifts the restoration; you are just ordering law and precedent to bring the realm under rule.

sentences.zh: 而琨受害非所，冤痛已甚，未聞朝廷有以甄論。

translations.literal: Yet Kun suffered harm not at proper place; wrongful pain already extreme—never heard the court had means to discriminate and discuss.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Liu Kun died wrongfully and his grievance runs deep—still the court has issued no judgment to set the record straight.

sentences.zh: 昔壺關三老訟衞太子之罪，-{谷}-永、劉向辨陳湯之功，下足以明功罪之分，上足以悟聖主之懷。

translations.literal: Formerly Huguan's three elders sued Prince Wei heir's guilt; Gu Yong and Liu Xiang distinguished Chen Tang's merit—below sufficient to clarify merit and guilt's distinction, above sufficient to awaken sagely ruler's breast.
translations.idiomatic: Once the three elders of Huguan indicted the crimes of the heir of Wei; Gu Yong and Liu Xiang defended Chen Tang's achievements—such pleas clarify right and wrong below and move the ruler above.

sentences.zh: 臣等祖考以來，世受殊遇，人侍翠幄，出簪彤管，弗克負荷，播越遐荒，與琨周旋，接事終始，是以仰慕三臣在昔之義，謹陳本末，冒以上聞，仰希聖朝曲賜哀察。

translations.literal: Your servants and others from ancestors and fathers onward, generations receiving special favor; entering served emerald curtains, exiting pinned vermilion tubes—unable to bear the burden, scattered to distant wastes; with Kun circled and wheeled, joining affairs beginning to end—therefore admiring three ministers' righteousness of former times, respectfully state beginning and end, risk upward hearing, look up hoping sagely court bend and grant pitying examination.
translations.idiomatic: Our families have enjoyed imperial favor for generations—attending the throne within and bearing credentials abroad—yet we fled to the frontier and stood by Liu Kun from first to last. In the spirit of those ancient memorialists we lay out the whole story at risk to ourselves and beg the court's compassionate review.

translations.literal: Closing markup for a formatted block in the Wikisource edition (no words).
translations.idiomatic: End of the third section of the memorial.

sentences.zh: 太子中庶子溫嶠又上疏理之，帝乃下詔曰：「」贈侍中、太尉，諡曰湣。

translations.literal: Palace aide to heir apparent Wen Jiao again submitted memorial vindicating him; the emperor then issued edict saying "" posthumously granting Palace Attendant and Grand Commandant, posthumous title Min.
translations.idiomatic: Palace aide to the heir apparent Wen Jiao also memorialized on Liu Kun's behalf; the emperor issued an edict posthumously appointing him Palace Attendant and Grand Commandant with the posthumous name Min.

sentences.zh: 琨少負志氣，有縱橫之才，善交勝己，而頗浮誇。

translations.literal: Kun in youth bore ambition and spirit, had strategist's talent, was good at befriending those who surpassed himself, yet was rather boastful.
translations.idiomatic: In youth Liu Kun was ambitious and talented in the strategist's vein; he sought out men greater than himself but could be boastful.

sentences.zh: 與范陽祖逖爲友，聞逖被用，與親故書曰：「吾枕戈待旦，志梟逆虜，常恐祖生先吾著鞭。

translations.literal: With Fanyang Zu Ti he was friend; hearing Ti was employed, he wrote to kin and old friends saying, "I pillow spear awaiting dawn, intent beheading rebel captives; always fear Zu Sheng will before me apply the whip.
translations.idiomatic: He was friends with Zu Di of Fanyang; when Zu received appointment Liu Kun wrote to friends, "I sleep with my spear beside me, ready to behead the rebels—yet I keep fearing Zu Di will strike before I do.

sentences.zh: 」其意氣相期如此。

translations.literal: Their intent and spirit mutually expected thus.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the rivalry that fired them both.

sentences.zh: 在晉陽，常爲胡騎所圍數重，城中窘迫無計，琨乃乘月登樓清嘯，賊聞之，皆淒然長歎。

translations.literal: At Jinyang, constantly surrounded by Hu riders in several layers, inside the city pressed tight without stratagem; Kun then rode the moon ascending a tower and whistled clearly; the bandits hearing it all mournfully long sighed.
translations.idiomatic: At Jinyang, Hu horsemen ringed the walls again and again while the city ran out of options. One moonlit night Liu Kun mounted a tower and gave a long, clear whistle—the besiegers heard it and sighed in sorrow.

sentences.zh: 中夜奏胡笳，賊又流涕歔欷，有懷土之切。

translations.literal: Midnight he played Hu reed-pipes; the bandits again shed tears and sobbed, having longing for native soil's keenness.
translations.idiomatic: At midnight he played the nomad pipes; the enemy wept and sobbed, hearts aching for home.

sentences.zh: 向曉復吹之，賊並棄圍而走。

translations.literal: Toward dawn again blew them; the bandits together abandoned siege and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Near dawn he played again, and the besiegers broke camp and fled.

sentences.zh: 子群嗣。

translations.literal: Son Qun succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Liu Qun inherited his rank.

sentences.zh: 琨子 群

translations.literal: Kun's son Qun.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Kun's son Liu Qun

sentences.zh: =群字公度，少拜廣武侯世子。

translations.literal: Equals sign precedes: Qun's courtesy name was Gongdu; in youth he was invested heir son of Marquis of Guangwu.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Qun, courtesy name Gongdu, was invested as heir to the marquisate of Guangwu while still young.

sentences.zh: 隨父在晉陽，遭逢寇亂，數領偏軍征討。

translations.literal: Following his father at Jinyang, encountering bandit turmoil, several times led detached armies on campaigns.
translations.idiomatic: He followed his father at Jinyang through years of raids and repeatedly commanded detachments on campaign.

sentences.zh: 性清慎，有裁斷，得士類歡心。

translations.literal: By nature sober and cautious, having decisive judgment, won gentry types' joyful hearts.
translations.idiomatic: Cool-headed and decisive, he won the confidence of the educated elite.

sentences.zh: 及琨爲匹磾所害，琨從事中郎盧諶等率餘眾奉群依末波。

translations.literal: When Kun was harmed by Pidi, Kun's administrative aides Lu Chen and others led remaining masses supporting Qun to rely on Mobo.
translations.idiomatic: After Duan Pidi killed Liu Kun, Lu Chen and the other staff led the survivors and Liu Qun to take refuge with Duan Mobo.

sentences.zh: 溫嶠前後表稱：「姨弟劉群，內弟崔悅、盧諶等，皆在末波中，翹首南望。

translations.literal: Wen Jiao before and after memorial stated: "Maternal cousin Liu Qun, brothers-in-law Cui Yue, Lu Chen and others—all are within Mobo, crane-neck south gazing.
translations.idiomatic: Wen Jiao memorialized repeatedly: "My cousins Liu Qun, Cui Yue, and Lu Chen remain with Mobo's force, craning their necks toward the south.

sentences.zh: 愚謂此等並有文思，於人之中少可湣惜。

translations.literal: I foolishly hold these together possess literary thought; among men somewhat deserving pity and regret.
translations.idiomatic: They are cultivated men who deserve sympathy—among the lost few merit pity.

sentences.zh: 如蒙錄召，繼絕興亡，則陛下更生之恩，望古無二。

translations.literal: If we receive enrollment summons, continuing severed and raising lost, then Your Majesty's again-born grace—looking to antiquity without second.
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty recalls them, you will rescue the stranded as only a renewer of lives—no precedent in history surpasses it.

sentences.zh: 」，成帝詔徵群等，爲末波兄弟愛其才，托以道險不遣。

translations.literal: "—Emperor Cheng issued edict summoning Qun and others; Mobo's brothers loved their talent and pleaded road peril not dispatching.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Cheng summoned Liu Qun and his companions, but Mobo's brothers prized their talents and refused to send them, citing the hazards of the journey.

sentences.zh: 石季龍滅遼西，群及諶、悅同沒胡中，季龍皆優禮之，以群爲中書令。

translations.literal: Shi Jilong extinguished Liaoxi; Qun together with Chen and Yue alike sank among Hu; Jilong all honored them with courtesy, making Qun palace secretary.
translations.idiomatic: When Shi Hu conquered Liaoxi, Liu Qun, Lu Chen, and Cui Yue fell into Hu hands; Shi Hu treated them generously and named Liu Qun director of the palace secretariat.

sentences.zh: 至冉閔敗後，群遇害。

translations.literal: When Ran Min was defeated after, Qun met harm and died.
translations.idiomatic: After Ran Min fell, Liu Qun was killed.

sentences.zh: 時勒及季龍得公卿人士多殺之，其見擢用，終至大官者，唯有河東裴憲，渤海石璞，滎陽鄭系，潁川荀綽，北地傅暢及群、悅、諶等十餘人而已。

translations.literal: At the time Shi Le and Jilong captured dukes and ministers and gentlemen mostly killed them; those seen promoted and employed, ending reaching great offices—only Hedong Pei Xian, Bohai Shi Pu, Xingyang Zheng Xi, Yingchuan Xun Chuo, Beidi Fu Chang and Qun, Yue, Chen and others slightly more than ten persons only.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Le and Shi Hu slaughtered most captured officials; only a dozen or so—such as Pei Xian of Hedong, Shi Pu of Bohai, Zheng Xi of Xingyang, Xun Chuo of Yingchuan, Fu Chang of Beidi, plus Liu Qun, Cui Yue, and Lu Chen—rose to high office.
