sentences.zh: 琨兄 輿

translations.literal: Kun's elder brother Yu.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Kun's elder brother Liu Yu

sentences.zh: =輿字慶孫。

translations.literal: Equals sign precedes: Yu's courtesy name was Qingsun.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu, courtesy name Qingsun,

sentences.zh: 雋朗有才局，與琨並尚書郭奕之甥，名著當時。

translations.literal: Elegant and bright, having talent and scope; together with Kun both were Minister Guo Yi's nephews; name illustrious in that time.
translations.idiomatic: He was brilliant and able, a nephew of Minister Guo Yi like Liu Kun, and his name shone in that generation.

sentences.zh: 京都爲之語曰：「洛中奕奕，慶孫、越石。

translations.literal: The capital for them made a saying: "Within Luoyang shining bright—Qingsun, Yueshi.
translations.idiomatic: The capital ran a rhyme: "In Luoyang the brightest lights are Qingsun and Yueshi.

sentences.zh: 」辟宰府尚書郎。

translations.literal: "—summoned ministerial headquarters gentleman clerk of the masters of writing.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned to serve as a gentleman of the masters of writing in the ministerial headquarters.

sentences.zh: 兄弟素侮孫秀，及趙王倫輔政，孫秀執權，並免其官。

translations.literal: The brothers always insulted Sun Xiu; when Prince Zhao Lun aided governance, Sun Xiu grasped power—together stripped their offices.
translations.idiomatic: The brothers had long mocked Sun Xiu; when Prince Zhao Sima Lun dominated the court and Sun Xiu seized power, both brothers were dismissed.

sentences.zh: 妹適倫世子荂，荂與秀不協，復以輿爲散騎侍郎。

translations.literal: Younger sister married Lun's heir son Fu; Fu and Xiu were not harmonious—again made Yu gentleman attendant at leisure.
translations.idiomatic: Their sister had married Sima Lun's heir Sima Fu; when Fu quarreled with Sun Xiu, Liu Yu was restored as gentleman attendant at leisure.

sentences.zh: 齊王冏輔政，以輿爲中書侍郎。

translations.literal: Prince Qi Jiong aided governance, making Yu palace attendant.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince of Qi Sima Jiong directed affairs, Liu Yu became palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 東海王越、范陽王虓之舉兵也，以輿爲潁川太守。

translations.literal: Prince Donghai Yue, Prince Fanyang Xiao's raising troops—made Yu Yingchuan governor.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Donghai Sima Yue and Prince of Fanyang Sima Xiao raised armies, Liu Yu was named governor of Yingchuan.

sentences.zh: 及河間王顒檄劉喬討虓於許昌，矯詔曰：「潁川太守劉輿迫協范王虓，距逆詔命，多樹私黨，擅劫郡縣，合聚兵眾。

translations.literal: When Prince Hejian Yong summoned Liu Qiao to punish Xiao at Xuchang, forged edict said: "Yingchuan governor Liu Yu coerced Prince Fan Wang Xiao, resisting rebellious edict command, many erected private factions, without authority seizing commanderies and counties, assembling gathered troop masses.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Hejian Sima Yong ordered Liu Qiao to strike Sima Xiao at Xuchang with a forged edict: "The governor of Yingchuan, Liu Yu, coerces Prince of Fanyang Sima Xiao, defies lawful orders, packs offices with cronies, hijacks counties without authority, and rallies troops.

sentences.zh: 輿兄弟昔因趙王婚親，擅弄權勢，凶狡無道，久應誅夷，以遇赦令，得全首領。

translations.literal: Yu brothers formerly because Prince Zhao marriage kin without authority played with power position, fierce and cunning without way—long ought have been executed and extirpated; because encountering amnesty order, obtained preserving heads.
translations.idiomatic: The Liu brothers once exploited ties to Prince Zhao to wield power—vicious and lawless men long overdue for execution—yet amnesties spared their heads.

sentences.zh: 小人不忌，爲惡日滋，輒用苟晞爲兗州，斷截王命。

translations.literal: Petty men without restraint, doing evil daily increasing—rashly employed Gou Xi as Yanzhou, cutting off kingly command.
translations.idiomatic: Restraint means nothing to them; their crimes mount—they promoted Gou Xi to Yanzhou and choke off the imperial command.

sentences.zh: 鎮南大將軍弘，平南將軍、彭城王釋，征東大將軍准，各勒所領，徑會許昌，與喬並力。

translations.literal: General Who Guards the South Hong, General Who Pacifies the South Prince Pengcheng Shi, General Who Conquers the East Zhun—each commanding what they lead, directly converge Xuchang, with Qiao combine strength.
translations.idiomatic: General Who Guards the South Liu Hong, General Who Pacifies the South Prince of Pengcheng Sima Shi, and General Who Conquers the East Sima Zhun are each to march their commands straight to Xuchang and join Liu Qiao.

sentences.zh: 今遣右將軍張方爲大都督，督建威將軍呂朗、陽平太守刁默，率步騎十萬，同會許昌，以除輿兄弟。

translations.literal: Now dispatch General of the Right Zhang Fang as grand commander-in-chief, supervising General Who Establishes Might Lü Lang, Yangping governor Diao Mo—lead infantry and cavalry hundred thousand, together converge Xuchang, to eliminate Yu brothers.
translations.idiomatic: Right general Zhang Fang is named supreme commander over General Who Establishes Might Lü Lang and Yangping governor Diao Mo; they will bring one hundred thousand foot and horse to Xuchang and destroy the Liu brothers.

sentences.zh: 敢有舉兵距違王命，誅及五族。

translations.literal: Those who dare raise troops resisting violating kingly command—punishment reaches five clans.
translations.idiomatic: Anyone who takes arms against this decree will suffer the five-clan penalty.

sentences.zh: 能殺輿兄弟送首者，封三千戸縣侯，賜絹五千匹。

translations.literal: Those able to kill Yu brothers sending heads—enfeoff three thousand household county marquis, award silk five thousand bolts.
translations.idiomatic: Kill the Liu brothers and deliver their heads and you will be made county marquis at three thousand households with five thousand bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 」虓之敗，輿與之俱奔河北。

translations.literal: "—Xiao's defeat; Yu together with him both fled north of He.
translations.idiomatic: When Sima Xiao lost, Liu Yu fled north into Hebei with him.

sentences.zh: 虓既鎮鄴，以輿爲征虜將軍、魏郡太守。

translations.literal: When Xiao already garrisoned Ye, made Yu general who conquers captives and Wei commandery governor.
translations.idiomatic: Once Sima Xiao secured Ye, he named Liu Yu general who conquers captives and governor of Wei commandery.

sentences.zh: 虓薨，東海王越將召之，或曰：「輿猶膩也，近則汙人。

translations.literal: Xiao died; Prince Donghai Yue about to summon him—someone said: "Yu is still like grease—near then soils people.
translations.idiomatic: After Sima Xiao died, Prince Donghai Sima Yue meant to summon Liu Yu; someone warned, "Liu Yu clings like grease—get too close and he stains you.

sentences.zh: 」及至，越疑而-{御}-之。

translations.literal: "—when arrived, Yue doubted yet {-yu-} him.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Yu arrived, Sima Yue hesitated—yet kept him on staff anyway.

sentences.zh: 輿密視天下兵簿及倉庫、牛馬、器械、水陸之形，皆默識之。

translations.literal: Yu secretly inspected realm's troop registers and granaries, oxen and horses, weapons and gear, water and land's forms—all silently memorized them.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu secretly reviewed national rosters, granaries, livestock, arms, and river and road routes until he knew them by heart.

sentences.zh: 是時軍國多事，每會議，自潘滔以下，莫知所對。

translations.literal: At this time army and state many affairs; whenever convened council, from Pan Tao downward, none knew how to answer.
translations.idiomatic: With army and court overwhelmed, meetings left even Pan Tao and those below speechless.

sentences.zh: 輿既見越，應機辯畫，越傾膝酬接，即以爲左長史。

translations.literal: Yu once saw Yue, responding to occasion debating plans; Yue leaned knees rewardingly receiving—immediately made senior clerk of the left.
translations.idiomatic: Once Liu Yu faced Sima Yue he answered every question with plans; Yue warmed to him at once and named him senior clerk of the left.

sentences.zh: 越既總錄，以輿爲上佐，賓客滿筵，文案盈機，遠近書記日有數千，終日不倦，或以夜繼之，皆人人歡暢，莫不悅附。

translations.literal: Yue once overall supervised records, making Yu chief aide—guests filled mats; documents overflowed desks; far and near letters and records daily had several thousand—whole day not weary, sometimes using night continue—all persons joyful and smooth, none not pleased to attach.
translations.idiomatic: As Sima Yue ran the realm he relied on Liu Yu as chief aide: guests packed his hall, paperwork buried his desk, and thousands of letters arrived daily—yet Yu worked day and night without tiring and kept everyone engaged.

sentences.zh: 命議如流，酬對款備，時人服其能，比之陳遵。

translations.literal: Commands and deliberations like flowing; responding pairs earnest and complete—people of the time admired his ability, compared him to Chen Zun.
translations.idiomatic: His orders ran like water and his replies were thorough; contemporaries ranked him with Chen Zun for sheer competence.

sentences.zh: 時稱越府有三才：潘滔大才，劉輿長才，裴邈清才。

translations.literal: At the time Yue's headquarters was called having three talents: Pan Tao great talent, Liu Yu long talent, Pei Miao clear talent.
translations.idiomatic: People said Sima Yue's headquarters held three gifts—Pan Tao's breadth, Liu Yu's reach, and Pei Miao's clarity.

sentences.zh: 越誅繆播、王延等，皆輿謀也。

translations.literal: Yue executed Miao Bo, Wang Yan and others—all Yu's stratagem.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Yue's execution of Miao Bo and Wang Yan was Liu Yu's doing.

sentences.zh: 延愛妾荊氏有音伎，延尚未殮，輿便娉之。

translations.literal: Yan's beloved concubine Lady Jing had music skill; Yan not yet coffined—Yu then betrothed her.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yan's favorite concubine Lady Jing was a musician; before Yan's body lay in the coffin Liu Yu took her as his bride.

sentences.zh: 未及迎，又爲太傅從事中郎王俊所爭奪。

translations.literal: Before arrived to welcome, again by grand tutor administrative aide Wang Jun was contested and seized.
translations.idiomatic: Before the wedding came off, grand tutor aide Wang Jun seized her for himself.

sentences.zh: 御史中丞傅宣劾奏，越不問輿，而免俊官。

translations.literal: Imperial secretary imperial counselor Fu Xuan impeached memorial; Yue did not question Yu but stripped Jun's office.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial counselor Fu Xuan impeached the affair; Sima Yue spared Liu Yu and dismissed Wang Jun instead.

sentences.zh: 輿乃説越，遣琨鎮并州，爲越北面之重。

translations.literal: Yu then persuaded Yue, dispatching Kun to garrison Bingzhou, becoming Yue's north face's weight.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu urged Sima Yue to send Liu Kun to hold Bingzhou as the northern anchor of his power.

sentences.zh: 洛陽未敗，病指疽卒，時年四十七。

translations.literal: Luoyang not yet defeated—sick finger boil died; at the time age forty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: Before Luoyang fell he died of a finger abscess at forty-seven.

sentences.zh: 追贈驃騎將軍。

translations.literal: Posthumously granted general of agile cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously named general of agile cavalry.

sentences.zh: 先有功封定襄侯，諡曰貞。

translations.literal: Earlier for merit enfeoffed Dingxiang marquis; posthumous title said Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier merit had earned him the marquisate of Dingxiang; his posthumous name was Zhen.

sentences.zh: 子演嗣。

translations.literal: Son Yan succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Liu Yan inherited the title.

translations.idiomatic: Subsection divider in the source layout.

sentences.zh: 輿子 演

translations.literal: Yu's son Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu's son Liu Yan

sentences.zh: 演字始仁。

translations.literal: Yan's courtesy name was Shiren.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yan, courtesy name Shiren,

sentences.zh: 初辟太尉掾，除尚書郎，以父憂去職。

translations.literal: First summoned grand commandant clerk; appointed gentleman of the masters of writing; because father's mourning left office.
translations.idiomatic: He began as clerk to the grand commandant, became gentleman of the masters of writing, then resigned for mourning.

sentences.zh: 服闋，襲爵，太傅、東海王越引爲主簿。

translations.literal: Mourning ended; inherited noble rank; grand tutor Prince Donghai Yue drew him as chief clerk.
translations.idiomatic: When mourning ended he inherited the title and Prince Donghai Sima Yue took him on as chief clerk.

sentences.zh: 遷太子中庶子，出爲陽平太守。

translations.literal: Transferred palace aide to heir apparent; went out as Yangping governor.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to palace aide to the heir apparent, then left the capital as governor of Yangping.

sentences.zh: 自洛奔琨，琨以爲輔國將軍、魏郡太守。

translations.literal: From Luoyang fled to Kun; Kun made him general who aids the state and Wei commandery governor.
translations.idiomatic: He fled Luoyang to Liu Kun, who named him general who aids the state and governor of Wei commandery.

sentences.zh: 琨將討石勒，以演領勇士千人，行北中郎將、兗州刺史，鎮廩丘。

translations.literal: Kun about to punish Shi Le—made Yan lead braves thousand men, acting north central-inspector general and Yanzhou inspector, garrisoned Linqiu.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Kun prepared to strike Shi Le he gave Liu Yan a thousand picked troops as acting north central-inspector general and inspector of Yanzhou, stationed at Linqiu.

sentences.zh: 演斬王桑，走趙固，得眾七千人。

translations.literal: Yan beheaded Wang Sang, routed Zhao Gu, obtained masses seven thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yan slew Wang Sang, drove off Zhao Gu, and recruited seven thousand men.

sentences.zh: 爲石勒所攻，演距戰，勒退。

translations.literal: Was attacked by Shi Le; Yan resisted battle; Le withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Le attacked him; Liu Yan held his ground and Shi Le pulled back.

sentences.zh: 元帝拜爲都督、後將軍，假節。

translations.literal: Emperor Yuan appointed him commander-in-chief and general of the rear, credential staff.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yuan named him area commander and general of the rear with credential staff.

sentences.zh: 後爲石季龍所圍，求救于邵續、段鴦，鴦騎救之，季龍走，隨鴦屯厭次，被害。

translations.literal: Afterward was besieged by Shi Jilong; sought rescue from Shao Xu and Duan Yang; Yang's riders rescued him; Jilong fled—followed Yang garrisoned Yanqi, met harm and died.
translations.idiomatic: Later Shi Hu besieged him; he called on Shao Xu and Duan Yang for relief—Duan Yang's cavalry broke the siege and Shi Hu withdrew. Liu Yan then joined Duan Yang at Yanqi and was killed.

sentences.zh: 弟胤爲琨引兵，路逢烏桓賊，戰沒。

translations.literal: Younger brother Yin for Kun led troops; on road encountered Wuhuan bandits—died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: His brother Liu Yin led troops for Liu Kun and fell fighting Wuhuan raiders on the march.

sentences.zh: 胤弟挹初爲太傅、東海王越掾，與琨俱被害。

translations.literal: Yin's younger brother Yi first was grand tutor Prince Donghai Yue's clerk—together with Kun both met harm and died.
translations.idiomatic: Younger brother Liu Yi had served Sima Yue as clerk and died with Liu Kun.

sentences.zh: 挹弟啟，啟弟述，與琨子群俱在末波中，後併入石季龍。

translations.literal: Yi's younger brother Qi, Qi's younger brother Shu—together with Kun's son Qun all were within Mobo; afterward together entered Shi Jilong.
translations.idiomatic: His brothers Liu Qi and Liu Shu, like Liu Qun, were with Mobo and later passed into Shi Hu's service.

sentences.zh: 啟爲季龍尚書僕射，後歸國，穆帝拜爲前將軍，加給事中。

translations.literal: Qi was Jilong's vice director of the masters of writing; afterward returned to state; Emperor Mu appointed general of the front, added imperial counselor.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Qi became Shi Hu's vice director of the masters of writing, later returned south; Emperor Mu named him general of the front and attached him to the palace as imperial counselor.

sentences.zh: ，隨中軍將軍殷浩北伐，爲姚襄所敗，啟戰沒。

translations.literal: He accompanied central army general Yin Hao on the northern expedition, was defeated by Yao Xiang, and Qi died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: He joined central army general Yin Hao's northern campaign, lost to Yao Xiang, and Liu Qi died in the fighting.

sentences.zh: 述爲季龍侍中，隨啟歸國，拜驍騎將軍。

translations.literal: Shu was Jilong's palace attendant; followed Qi returned to state; appointed general of fierce cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Shu had been Shi Hu's palace attendant; he followed Liu Qi south and was named general of fierce cavalry.

sentences.zh: 祖逖

translations.literal: Zu Ti.
translations.idiomatic: Zu Ti

sentences.zh: 祖逖，字士稚，范陽遒人也。

translations.literal: Zu Ti, courtesy name Shizhi, was a man of Qiu in Fanyang.
translations.idiomatic: Zu Ti, courtesy name Shizhi, came from Qiu in Fanyang.

sentences.zh: 世吏二千石，爲北州舊姓。

translations.literal: Generations officials two thousand piculs—was northern province old surname.
translations.idiomatic: For generations his family held salary rank at two thousand piculs—a distinguished northern clan.

sentences.zh: 父武，晉王掾上-{谷}-太守。

translations.literal: Father Wu—Prince of Jin clerk Shang-{gu}- governor.
translations.idiomatic: His father Zu Wu had served as clerk to the prince of Jin and governor of Shang-{gu}-.

sentences.zh: 逖少孤，兄弟六人。

translations.literal: Ti in youth orphaned; brothers six men.
translations.idiomatic: Zu Ti lost his father young and had five brothers.

sentences.zh: 兄該、納等並開爽有才幹。

translations.literal: Elder brothers Gai, Na and others together open bright having talent and capacity.
translations.idiomatic: His brothers Zu Gai, Zu Na, and the rest were open-hearted men of ability.

sentences.zh: 逖性豁蕩，不修儀檢，年十四五猶未知書，諸兄每憂之。

translations.literal: Ti's nature broad and unrestrained, did not cultivate ritual restraint—age fourteen five still not knew writing; elder brothers always worried him.
translations.idiomatic: Zu Ti was freewheeling and careless of etiquette; at fourteen or fifteen he still barely read, and his brothers worried.

sentences.zh: 然輕財好俠，慷慨有節尚，每至田舍，輒稱兄意，散穀帛以周貧乏，鄉黨宗族以是重之。

translations.literal: Yet slighted wealth loved knight-errantry, generous having moral preference—whenever arrived village farms, always claimed elder brothers' intent, scattering grain and silk to relieve poverty—village and clan therefore esteemed him.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he spurned riches and loved bold deeds; visiting the countryside he would invoke his brothers' names and give grain and cloth to the needy—kinsmen and neighbors respected him for it.

sentences.zh: 後乃博覽書記，該涉古今，往來京師，見者謂逖有贊世才具。

translations.literal: Afterward then broadly viewed documents and records, comprehended pervaded ancient and modern, traveled back and forth capital—those who saw said Ti had aid-the-age talent implements.
translations.idiomatic: Later he read widely in letters and history; traveling to the capital he was hailed as a man fit to rescue the age.

sentences.zh: 僑居陽平。

translations.literal: Sojourned dwelling Yangping.
translations.idiomatic: He lived as a guest in Yangping.

sentences.zh: 年二十四，陽平辟察孝廉，司隸再辟舉秀才，皆不行。

translations.literal: Age twenty-four—Yangping summoned investigated filial and incorrupt; metropolitan commandant again summoned recommended flourishing talent—all did not go.
translations.idiomatic: At twenty-four Yangping nominated him as filial and incorrupt and the metropolitan command recommended him as flourishing talent—he declined both.

sentences.zh: 與司空劉琨俱爲司州主簿，情好綢繆，共被同寢。

translations.literal: Together with Minister Liu Kun both were Sizhou chief clerk—feelings good intimate tangled, shared quilt same sleeping.
translations.idiomatic: He and Minister Liu Kun both served as chief clerk of Sizhou; they were inseparable bedmates under one quilt.

sentences.zh: 中夜聞荒雞鳴，蹴琨覺曰：「此非惡聲也。

translations.literal: Midnight heard wild cock crow—kicked Kun awake saying: "This is not ill sound.
translations.idiomatic: One midnight a stray cock crowed; Zu Ti kicked Liu Kun awake and said, "That is no ill omen.

sentences.zh: 」因起舞。

translations.literal: "—thereupon rose and danced.
translations.idiomatic: They got up and danced.

sentences.zh: 逖、琨並有英氣，每語世事，或中宵起坐，相謂曰：「若四海鼎沸，豪傑並起，吾與足下當相避于中原耳。」

translations.literal: Ti and Kun together had heroic spirit; whenever discussed world's affairs, sometimes midnight rose and sat, mutually said: "If four seas cauldron boiling, heroes together rise—you and I ought mutually avoid each other in central plain ear.
translations.idiomatic: Both men burned with ambition; talking politics at midnight they would sit up and say, "If the realm boils over and heroes rise everywhere, you and I had best watch each other on the Central Plain.

sentences.zh: 辟齊王冏大司馬掾、長沙王乂驃騎祭酒，轉主簿，累遷太子中舍人、豫章王從事中郎。

translations.literal: Summoned Prince Qi Jiong grand marshal clerk, Prince Changsha Yi swift-rider libationer—transferred chief clerk, accumulated transferred heir apparent central lodge man, Prince Yuzhang administrative aide.
translations.idiomatic: He served Prince of Qi as clerk to the grand marshal and Prince of Changsha as libationer to the swift-rider general, moved to chief clerk, then rose to attendant of the heir and administrative aide to the prince of Yuzhang.

sentences.zh: 從惠帝北伐，王師敗績于蕩陰，遂退還洛。

translations.literal: Followed Emperor Hui northern expedition—royal army defeated at Dangyin—thereupon withdrew returned Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: He joined Emperor Hui's northern campaign; after the rout at Dangyin he pulled back to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 大駕西幸長安，關東諸侯范陽王虓、高密王略、平昌公模等競召之，皆不就。

translations.literal: Great carriage west favored Chang'an—east-of-pass lords Prince Fanyang Xiao, Prince Gaomi Lüe, Duke Pingchang Mo and others competed summoning him—all did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: When the court fled west to Chang'an, Prince of Fanyang, Prince of Gaomi, Duke Pingchang, and other lords east of the pass vied to enlist him—he refused every offer.

sentences.zh: 東海王越以逖爲典兵參軍、濟陰太守，母喪不之官。

translations.literal: Prince Donghai Yue made Ti oversee-armies army adviser and Jiyin governor—mother's mourning did not take office.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Donghai Sima Yue named him army adviser and governor of Jiyin, but mourning for his mother kept him from taking post.

sentences.zh: 及京師大亂，逖率親黨數百家避地淮泗，以所乘車馬載同行老疾，躬自徒步，藥物衣糧與眾共之，又多權略，是以少長咸宗之，推逖爲行主。

translations.literal: When capital great chaos—Ti led kin and associates several hundred families fleeing territory Huai and Si—used what rode carriages and horses load traveling together old and sick—personally himself walked on foot—medicine goods clothing grain shared with masses together—also much stratagem—therefore young and old all honored him, pushed Ti as march chief.
translations.idiomatic: When Luoyang collapsed he led hundreds of kinsmen toward Huai and Si: he put the aged and infirm in his carts and walked himself, sharing medicine and food—his resourcefulness won every age, and they chose him head of the column.

sentences.zh: 達泗口，元帝拟用爲徐州刺史，尋徵軍諮祭酒，居丹徒之京口。

translations.literal: Reached Sikou—Emperor Yuan planned use him as Xuzhou inspector—shortly summoned army consultation libationer—dwelt Dantu’s Jingkou.
translations.idiomatic: At Sikou Emperor Yuan meant to make him inspector of Xuzhou, then recalled him as libationer for army consultation and housed him at Jingkou in Dantu.

sentences.zh: 逖以社稷傾覆，常懷振復之志。

translations.literal: Ti because altars overturned—always cherished restore-and-recover intent.
translations.idiomatic: With the dynastic altars in ruins Zu Ti burned to reconquer the north.

sentences.zh: 賓客義徒皆暴傑勇士，逖遇之如子弟。

translations.literal: Guests and righteous followers all violent heroes brave men—Ti treated them like sons and younger brothers.
translations.idiomatic: His followers were rugged fighters; he treated them like family.

sentences.zh: 時揚土大饑，此輩多爲盜竊，攻剽富室，逖撫慰問之曰：「比復南塘一出不？

translations.literal: At time Yang soil great famine—these kinds mostly became thieves and robbers, attacking plundering rich houses—Ti soothed and asked them saying: "Recently again south pond one outing or not?
translations.idiomatic: Famine stalked the south; many of his men turned to raiding the rich. Zu Ti only smiled and asked, "Another night raid on South Bank mansions?

sentences.zh: 」或爲吏所繩，逖輒擁護救解之。

translations.literal: "—some were by clerks bound by law—Ti always shielded protected rescued them.
translations.idiomatic: When officials moved against them, he shielded his men.

sentences.zh: 談者以此少逖，然自若也。

translations.literal: Discussers for this slighted Ti—yet self-composed also.
translations.idiomatic: Critics thought less of him for it; he remained unconcerned.

sentences.zh: 時帝方拓定江南，未遑北伐，逖進説曰：「晉室之亂，非上無道而下怨叛也。

translations.literal: At time emperor just expanding settling Jiangnan—not leisure northern expedition—Ti advanced persuasion saying: "Jin house's turmoil—not above without way and below resentful rebel.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was still securing the south, so Zu Ti urged him: "The Jin collapse did not come because the throne lacked virtue and the people turned traitor.

sentences.zh: 由籓王爭權，自相誅滅，遂使戎狄乘隙，毒流中原。

translations.literal: Because feudal kings strove for power, mutually slaughtered and extinguished—thereupon caused Rong and Di seize cracks—poison flowed central plain.
translations.idiomatic: Princely rivals tore one another apart and gave the nomads their opening—poison spread across the Central Plain.

sentences.zh: 今遺黎既被殘酷，人有奮擊之志。

translations.literal: Now surviving black-haired already suffer cruel brutality—men have strike-out intent.
translations.idiomatic: The survivors have tasted cruelty; every heart yearns to strike back.

sentences.zh: 大王誠能發威命將，使若逖等爲之統主，則郡國豪傑必因風向赴，沈弱之士欣于來蘇，庶幾國恥可雪，願大王圖之。

translations.literal: Great king truly able issue awesome command generals—cause such as Ti and others be their chief leaders—then commandery and state heroes must ride wind direction hasten; sunk weak gentlemen rejoice at coming revival—perhaps state's shame may be wiped—wish great king plan it.
translations.idiomatic: If Your Highness will issue orders and let men like me lead, regional heroes will rally to the wind, the downtrodden will rejoice at deliverance, and the nation's shame may yet be avenged—I beg you to consider it.

sentences.zh: 」帝乃以逖爲奮威將軍、豫州刺史，給千人稟，布三千匹，不給鎧仗，使自招募。

translations.literal: "—Emperor then made Ti general who rouses might and Yuzhou inspector—granted thousand men rations, cloth three thousand bolts—not granting armor weapons—ordered self recruit.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor named Zu Ti general who rouses might and inspector of Yuzhou with rations for one thousand men and three thousand bolts of cloth—no arms or armor—and told him to raise the rest himself.

sentences.zh: 仍將本流徙部曲百餘家渡江，中流擊楫而誓曰：「」辭色壯烈，眾皆慨歎。

translations.literal: Still led original drifting-retainer households hundred-plus families cross river—midstream beat oars and swore saying: "If Ti cannot clear central plain and again cross—like great river!"—word and color fierce splendid—all sighed with emotion.
translations.idiomatic: He led his hundred-odd refugee households across the Yangzi; midstream he struck the oar and swore, "If I fail to recover the Central Plain and return across this river, may the Yangzi sweep me away like this paddle!" His voice shook his followers to tears.

sentences.zh: 屯于江陰，起冶鑄兵器，得二千餘人而後進。

translations.literal: Encamped at Jiangyin; raised smelting furnace casting weapons; obtained two thousand-plus men and afterward advanced.
translations.idiomatic: He camped at Jiangyin, forged arms, and recruited over two thousand fighters before pushing inland.

sentences.zh: 初，北中郎將劉演距于石勒也，流人塢主張平、樊雅等在譙，演署平爲豫州刺史，雅爲譙郡太守。

translations.literal: Earlier, north central-inspector general Liu Yan resisted Shi Le—drifting people's fort chiefs Zhang Ping, Fan Ya and others were at Qiao; Yan appointed Ping as Yuzhou inspector and Ya as Qiao commandery governor.
translations.idiomatic: While Liu Yan held Shi Le at bay, refugee fort leaders Zhang Ping and Fan Ya controlled Qiao—Liu Yan named Zhang Ping inspector of Yuzhou and Fan Ya governor of Qiao commandery.

sentences.zh: 又有董瞻、于武、謝浮等十餘部，眾各數百，皆統屬平。

translations.literal: Also were Dong Zhan, Yu Wu, Xie Fu and others ten-plus bands—masses each several hundred—all unified subordinate to Ping.
translations.idiomatic: More than a dozen bands led by Dong Zhan, Yu Wu, Xie Fu, each a few hundred strong, all answered to Zhang Ping.

sentences.zh: 逖誘浮使取平，浮譎平與會，遂斬以獻逖。

translations.literal: Ti enticed Fu to make him seize Ping; Fu deceived Ping to meet—thereupon beheaded and presented to Ti.
translations.idiomatic: Zu Ti persuaded Xie Fu to eliminate Zhang Ping; Fu lured Zhang Ping to a meeting, slew him, and sent his head to Zu Ti.

sentences.zh: 帝嘉逖勳，使運糧給之，而道遠不至，軍中大饑。

translations.literal: Emperor praised Ti's merit—ordered transport grain supply him—but road far did not arrive—army inside great famine.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor honored Zu Ti's service and ordered grain sent, but it never arrived—the army starved.

sentences.zh: 進據太丘。

translations.literal: Advanced and occupied Taiqiu.
translations.idiomatic: He advanced and seized Taiqiu.

sentences.zh: 樊雅遣眾夜襲逖，遂入壘，拔戟大呼，直趣逖幕，軍土大亂。

translations.literal: Fan Ya sent masses night raid Ti—thereupon entered rampart, drew halberd great shouted—straight rushed Ti's tent—army earth great chaos.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Ya struck by night: his men burst the camp, brandished halberds, and drove straight for Zu Ti's headquarters until the lines broke.

sentences.zh: 逖命左右距之，督護董昭與賊戰，走之。

translations.literal: Ti ordered left and right resist them—protector Dong Zhao battled bandits—routed them.
translations.idiomatic: Zu Ti ordered a counterattack; protector Dong Zhao fought and drove the raiders off.

sentences.zh: 逖率眾追討，而張平餘眾助雅攻逖。

translations.literal: Ti led masses pursue punish—but Zhang Ping remainder masses aided Ya attacking Ti.
translations.idiomatic: Zu Ti pressed the pursuit while Zhang Ping's survivors joined Fan Ya against him.

sentences.zh: 蓬陂塢主陳川，自號甯朔將軍、陳留太守。

translations.literal: Pengpi fort chief Chen Chuan—self-styled General Who Pacifies the North and Chenliu governor.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Chuan of the Pengpi fort styled himself general who pacifies the north and governor of Chenliu.

sentences.zh: 逖遣使求救於川，川遣將李頭率眾援之，逖遂克譙城。

translations.literal: Ti dispatched envoy seek rescue from Chuan; Chuan sent general Li Tou lead masses aid him—Ti thereupon overcame Qiao city.
translations.idiomatic: Zu Ti begged Chen Chuan for help; Chen sent Li Tou with reinforcements, and Zu Ti took Qiao.

sentences.zh: 初，樊雅之據譙也，逖以力弱，求助於南中郎將王含，含遣桓宣領兵助逖。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Fan Ya held Qiao, Ti because strength weak sought aid from south central-inspector general Wang Han—Han sent Huan Xuan lead troops aid Ti.
translations.idiomatic: When Fan Ya first held Qiao, Zu Ti was too weak and begged south central-inspector Wang Han for troops; Wang sent Huan Xuan to his aid.

sentences.zh: 逖既克譙，宣等乃去。

translations.literal: Ti once overcame Qiao, Xuan and others then departed.
translations.idiomatic: After Qiao fell, Huan Xuan withdrew.

sentences.zh: 石季龍聞而引眾圍譙，含又遣宣救逖，季龍聞宣至而退。

translations.literal: Shi Jilong heard and led masses besiege Qiao—Han again sent Xuan rescue Ti—Jilong heard Xuan arrived and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Hu besieged Qiao in response; Wang Han sent Huan Xuan again, and Shi Hu retreated when he arrived.

sentences.zh: 宣遂留，助逖討諸屯塢未附者。

translations.literal: Xuan thereupon remained—aided Ti punish various fort garrisons not yet attached.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Xuan stayed to help Zu Ti reduce the forts that still held out.

sentences.zh: 李頭之討樊雅也，力戰有勳。

translations.literal: Li Tou's punishing Fan Ya—fought hard having merit.
translations.idiomatic: Li Tou had fought Fan Ya with distinction.

sentences.zh: 逖時獲雅駿馬，頭甚欲之而不敢言，逖知其意，遂與之。

translations.literal: Ti at time captured Ya's swift horse—Tou greatly desired it but dared not speak—Ti knew his intent—thereupon gave it.
translations.idiomatic: Zu Ti had taken Fan Ya's fine horse; Li Tou longed for it in silence until Zu Ti read his wish and gave him the mount.

sentences.zh: 頭感逖恩遇，每歎曰：「若得此人爲主，吾死無恨。

translations.literal: Tou felt Ti's grace meeting—always sighed saying: "If obtain this man as lord—I die without regret.
translations.idiomatic: Grateful for Zu Ti's kindness, Li Tou often said, "If only he were my commander—I could die content.

sentences.zh: 」川聞而怒，遂殺頭。

translations.literal: "—Chuan heard and angry—thereupon killed Tou.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Chuan heard and murdered Li Tou in rage.

sentences.zh: 頭親黨馮寵率其屬四百入歸於逖，川益怒，遣將魏碩掠豫州諸郡，大獲子女車馬。

translations.literal: Tou's kin party Feng Chong led his following four hundred enter submit to Ti—Chuan more angry—sent general Wei Shuo plunder Yuzhou various commanderies—greatly captured women children carriages horses.
translations.idiomatic: Li Tou's kinsman Feng Chong brought four hundred followers to Zu Ti; Chen Chuan raged and sent Wei Shuo to ravage Yuzhou, seizing people and stock.

sentences.zh: 逖遣將軍衞策邀擊于-{谷}-水，盡獲所掠者，皆令歸本，軍無私焉。

translations.literal: Ti sent general Wei Ce intercept strike at Gu water—wholly captured what was plundered—all ordered return native—army had no private seizure.
translations.idiomatic: Zu Ti's general Wei Ce ambushed Wei Shuo at the Gu River, recovered every captive, sent them home, and kept nothing for the army.

sentences.zh: 川大懼，遂以眾附石勒。

translations.literal: Chuan greatly feared—thereupon with masses attached Shi Le.
translations.idiomatic: Terror drove Chen Chuan to surrender his force to Shi Le.

sentences.zh: 逖率眾伐川，石季龍領兵五萬救川，逖設奇以擊之，季龍大敗，收兵掠豫州，徙陳川還襄國，留桃豹等守川故城，住西臺。

translations.literal: Ti led masses attack Chuan—Shi Jilong led troops fifty thousand rescue Chuan—Ti set ambush to strike him—Jilong great defeat—gathered troops plunder Yuzhou—relocated Chen Chuan back Xiangguo—left Tao Bao and others guard Chuan's old city—dwelt west tower.
translations.idiomatic: Zu Ti marched on Chen Chuan; Shi Hu brought fifty thousand men and lost to Zu Ti's ruse. Shi Hu pulled back through Yuzhou, shipped Chen Chuan to Xiangguo, left Tao Bao to hold the old fort on the west mound.

sentences.zh: 逖遣將韓潛等鎮東臺。

translations.literal: Ti sent generals Han Qian and others garrison east tower.
translations.idiomatic: Zu Ti posted Han Qian on the east mound.

sentences.zh: 同一大城，賊從南門出入放牧，逖軍開東門，相守四旬。

translations.literal: Same one great wall—bandits from south gate exit enter pasture herds—Ti's army opened east gate—mutually guarded forty days.
translations.idiomatic: Within one walled city the enemy used the south gate to herd livestock while Zu Ti held the east gate; the standoff lasted forty days.

sentences.zh: 逖以布囊盛土如米狀，使千餘人運上臺，又令數人擔米，偽爲疲極而息於道，賊果逐之，皆棄擔而走。

translations.literal: Ti used cloth sacks fill earth like rice shape—made thousand-plus men transport up tower—also ordered several men shoulder rice—feigned exhausted extreme and rest on road—bandits indeed chased them—all abandoned shoulder loads and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Zu Ti filled sacks with earth to look like grain and had men haul them up the mound; others carried real rice and feigned exhaustion by the road. When the enemy rushed them they dropped the loads and fled.

sentences.zh: 賊既獲米，謂逖士眾豐飽，而胡戍饑久，益懼，無復膽氣。

translations.literal: Bandits once obtained rice—thought Ti's soldiers masses abundant full—but Hu garrison starved long—more fearful—no again gall courage.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing the grain, the enemy assumed Zu Ti's men were well fed while their own Hu troops had starved so long they lost heart.

sentences.zh: 石勒將劉夜堂以驢千頭運糧以饋桃豹，逖遣韓潛、馮鐵等追擊于汴水，盡獲之。

translations.literal: Shi Le general Liu Yetang used donkeys thousand head transport grain to feed Tao Bao—Ti sent Han Qian, Feng Tie and others pursue strike at Bian water—wholly captured them.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Le's officer Liu Yetang drove a thousand donkeys of supplies to Tao Bao; Han Qian and Feng Tie ambushed them on the Bian River and seized everything.

sentences.zh: 豹宵遁，退據東燕城，逖使潛進屯封丘以逼之。

translations.literal: Bao night fled—withdrew occupy Dongyan city—Ti made Qian advance garrison Fengqiu to press him.
translations.idiomatic: Tao Bao slipped away by night to Dongyan; Zu Ti pushed Han Qian forward at Fengqiu to squeeze him.

sentences.zh: 馮鐵據二臺，逖鎮雍丘，數遣軍要截石勒，勒屯戍漸蹙。

translations.literal: Feng Tie held two towers—Ti garrisoned Yongqiu—several times sent armies intercept Shi Le—Le garrison posts gradually cramped.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Tie held both mounds while Zu Ti headquartered at Yongqiu, repeatedly cutting Shi Le's lines until Le's garrisons shrank.

sentences.zh: 候騎常獲濮陽人，逖厚待遣歸。

translations.literal: Scout riders often captured Puyang people—Ti thickly treated sent return.
translations.idiomatic: Patrols often took men from Puyang; Zu Ti treated them well and sent them home.

sentences.zh: 咸感逖恩德，率鄉里五百家降逖。

translations.literal: All felt Ti's grace virtue—led villages five hundred households submit Ti.
translations.idiomatic: Grateful for his kindness, five hundred local households came over to him.

sentences.zh: 勒又遣精騎萬人距逖，復爲逖所破，勒鎮戍歸附者甚多。

translations.literal: Le again sent crack riders ten thousand resist Ti—again by Ti was defeated—Le's garrison posts submitting attached very many.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Le sent ten thousand picked horsemen and lost again; ever more of his border posts defected.

sentences.zh: 時趙固、上官巳、李矩、郭默等各以詐力相攻擊，逖遣使和解之，示以禍福，遂受逖節度。

translations.literal: At time Zhao Gu, Shangguan Si, Li Ju, Guo Mo and others each by deceit strength mutually attacked—Ti sent envoys reconcile them—showed them fortune and disaster—thereupon received Ti's command control.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Gu, Shangguan Si, Li Ju, and Guo Mo were raiding one another; Zu Ti mediated, explained costs and gains, and brought them under his command.

sentences.zh: 逖愛人下士，雖疏交賤隸，皆恩禮遇之，由是黃河以南盡爲晉土。

translations.literal: Ti loved men lowered scholars—even distant associates mean slaves—all grace and ritual treated them—thereby Yellow River south of entirely became Jin soil.
translations.idiomatic: Zu Ti honored talent and humored common soldiers alike—every humble ally received courtesy—until south of the Yellow River flew Jin banners.

sentences.zh: 河上堡固先有任子在胡者，皆聽兩屬，時遣遊軍偽抄之，明其未附。

translations.literal: River on fortifications originally had hostages in Hu—all heard double attachment—occasionally sent roaming troops feigned raid them—clarify their not attached.
translations.idiomatic: River forts with hostages held by the Hu were allowed to serve both sides; Zu Ti sent raiders to strike them in pretense, proving they had not truly submitted to the enemy.

sentences.zh: 諸塢主感戴，胡中有異謀，輒密以聞。

translations.literal: Fort chiefs grateful—among Hu when had different plot—always secretly informed.
translations.idiomatic: Fort commanders repaid him with loyalty and leaked every Hu intrigue.

sentences.zh: 前後克獲，亦由此也。

translations.literal: Before and after victories captures—also from this.
translations.idiomatic: His victories owed much to that network.

translations.literal: Those who had slight merit—reward not exceed day.
translations.idiomatic: The smallest merit earned reward within the day.

sentences.zh: 躬自儉約，勸督農桑，克己務施，不畜資產，子弟耕耘，負擔樵薪，又收葬枯骨，爲之祭醊，百姓感悅。

translations.literal: Personally self frugal—urged supervised farming and mulberry—restrained self devoted to giving—not hoarded assets—sons and younger brothers plowed—shouldered burdens firewood—also gathered buried dry bones—for them offered libation sacrifice—hundred surnames felt joy.
translations.idiomatic: He lived plainly, pushed farming, gave away what little he had, kept no estates, made kin till the soil and gather fuel, buried the dead with offerings—the people loved him.

sentences.zh: 嘗置酒大會，耆老中坐流涕曰：「吾等老矣！

translations.literal: Once set wine great assembly—elders middle sat shedding tears saying: "We are old!
translations.idiomatic: At a banquet the elders wept in their midst: "We are old!

sentences.zh: 更得父母，死將何恨！

translations.literal: Again obtain father mother—what regret in death!
translations.idiomatic: Yet we have found parents again—what is death to us now!

sentences.zh: 」乃歌曰：「幸哉遺黎免俘虜，三辰既朗遇慈父，玄酒忘勞甘瓠脯，何以詠恩歌且舞。

translations.literal: "—thereupon sang saying: "Fortunate surviving black-haired escape captivity—three luminaries already bright meet kind father—dark wine forget toil sweet gourd dried meat—with what chant grace sing and dance.
translations.idiomatic: They sang: "The spared people quit bondage; sun, moon, and stars shine again under a gentle father; plain wine and gourd meat erase our toil—how else repay him but in song and dance!

sentences.zh: 」其得人心如此。

translations.literal: "—his obtaining people's hearts thus.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the hold he had on hearts.

sentences.zh: 故劉琨與親故書，盛讚逖威德。

translations.literal: Therefore Liu Kun to kin and old friends letter—greatly praised Ti's might and virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Kun wrote home praising Zu Ti's prestige and kindness.

sentences.zh: 詔進逖爲鎮西將軍。

translations.literal: Edict advanced Ti to general who garrisons the west.
translations.idiomatic: An edict promoted him to general who garrisons the west.

sentences.zh: 石勒不敢窺兵河南，使成皋縣修逖母墓，因與逖書，求通使交市，逖不報書，而聽互市，收利十倍，於是公私豐贍，士馬日滋。

translations.literal: Shi Le did not dare spy troops south of river—ordered Chenggao county repair Ti mother's tomb—thereby wrote Ti letter—sought exchange envoys trade market—Ti did not reply letter—but heard mutual market—collected profit tenfold—thereupon public and private abundantly supplied—soldiers and horses daily increased.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Le dared not probe Henan; he had Zu Ti's mother's tomb tended at Chenggao and wrote seeking envoys and trade. Zu Ti ignored the letter yet allowed border markets—profits multiplied tenfold—state and army alike grew rich.

sentences.zh: 方當推鋒越河，掃清冀朔，會朝廷將遣戴若思爲都督，逖以若思是吳人，雖有才望，無弘致遠識，且已翦荊棘，收河南地，而若思雍容，一旦來統之，意甚怏怏。

translations.literal: Just about to push blades cross river—sweep clear Ji and Shuo—happened court about to send Dai Ruosi as commander-in-chief—Ti because Ruosi was Wu man—although had talent renown—lacked vast reach far insight—and already cut brambles—recovered south-of-river land—but Ruosi graceful ease—once came command them—intent very disgruntled.
translations.idiomatic: He was ready to vault the Yellow River and clear Ji and the northern plain when the court meant to send Dai Ruosi as overall commander. Dai was a Wu man of reputation but no breadth of vision; Zu Ti had cleared thorns and reclaimed Henan—yet a polished outsider would suddenly command him, and his heart sank.

sentences.zh: 且聞王敦與劉隗等構隙，慮有內難，大功不遂。

translations.literal: Moreover heard Wang Dun and Liu Wei and others built rift—feared would have internal calamity—great merit not succeed.
translations.idiomatic: Word that Wang Dun and Liu Wei were at odds warned him of civil strife—his great project might fail.

sentences.zh: 感激發病，乃致妻孥汝南大木山下。

translations.literal: Stirred sick illness—thereupon sent wife and children Runan great tree mountain below.
translations.idiomatic: Grief and rage broke his health; he moved his family to the foot of Mount Damu in Runan.

sentences.zh: 時中原士庶咸謂逖當進據武牢，而反置家險厄，或諫之，不納。

translations.literal: At time central plain scholars and commoners all said Ti ought advance occupy Wu'ao—but contrary settled family in peril—some remonstrated—not accepted.
translations.idiomatic: Northerners expected Zu Ti to seize Wulao Pass; instead he parked his family in danger—advisers protested in vain.

sentences.zh: 逖雖內懷憂憤，而圖進取不輟，營繕武牢城，城北臨黃河，西接成皋，四望甚遠。

translations.literal: Ti although inside harbored worry and rage—yet plotted advance without cease—built repair Wu'ao city—city north faced Yellow River—west joined Chenggao—four views very far.
translations.idiomatic: Though sick at heart he kept planning offensives, rebuilt Wulao town above the Yellow River facing Chenggao with views far in every direction.

sentences.zh: 逖恐南無堅壘，必爲賊所襲，乃使從子汝南太守濟率汝陽太守張敞、新蔡內史周閎率眾築壘。

translations.literal: Ti feared south had no firm rampart—must by bandits be raided—therefore ordered nephew Runan governor Ji lead Ruyang governor Zhang Chang, Xincai interior secretary Zhou Hong lead masses build rampart.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing no strong southern bastion would tempt raiders, he told his nephew Ji—governor of Runan—and governors Zhang Chang and Zhou Hong to raise fortifications.

sentences.zh: 未成，而逖病甚。

translations.literal: Not completed—but Ti illness severe.
translations.idiomatic: Before the works finished Zu Ti fell gravely ill.

sentences.zh: 先是，華譚、庾闡問術人戴洋，洋曰：「祖豫州九月當死。

translations.literal: Earlier, Hua Tan, Yu Chan questioned technician Dai Yang—Yang said: "Grand Protector of Yu Zhou ninth month ought die.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Hua Tan and Yu Chan had asked the diviner Dai Yang, who said, "Grand Protector Zu will die in the ninth month.

sentences.zh: 」初有妖星見於豫州之分，曆陽陳訓又謂人曰：「今年西北大將當死。

translations.literal: "—Earlier had baleful star appear at Yuzhou's division—Liyang Chen Xun again told people saying: "This year northwest great general ought die.
translations.idiomatic: A comet had appeared over Yuzhou's sky; Chen Xun of Liyang told folk, "This year a great general of the northwest will die.

sentences.zh: 」逖亦見星，曰：「爲我矣！

translations.literal: "—Ti also saw star—said: "For me!
translations.idiomatic: Zu Ti saw the portent too and said, "That means me!

sentences.zh: 方平河北，而天欲殺我，此乃不祐國也。

translations.literal: Just pacifying Hebei—but Heaven wishes kill me—this is not blessing state.
translations.idiomatic: The north was nearly pacified, yet Heaven would cut me down—the realm goes unwatched.

sentences.zh: 」俄卒於雍丘，時年五十六。

translations.literal: "—soon died at Yongqiu—at the time age fifty-six.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he died at Yongqiu at fifty-six.

sentences.zh: 豫州士女若喪考妣，譙梁百姓爲之立祠。

translations.literal: Yuzhou gentlemen and women as if lost father mother—Qiao and Liang hundred surnames for him erected shrines.
translations.idiomatic: Yuzhou mourned like orphaned children; Qiao and Liang built shrines to him.

sentences.zh: 冊贈車騎將軍。

translations.literal: Patent posthumously granted chariot and cavalry general.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumous patent named him chariot and cavalry general.

sentences.zh: 王敦久懷逆亂，畏逖不敢發，至是始得肆意焉。

translations.literal: Wang Dun long harbored rebellious turmoil—feared Ti dared not erupt—at this then obtained indulge whim.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dun had long plotted rebellion but feared Zu Ti; only now could he proceed unchecked.

sentences.zh: 尋以逖弟約代領其眾。

translations.literal: Shortly used Ti's younger brother Yue replace lead his masses.
translations.idiomatic: Zu Yue soon succeeded him in command.

sentences.zh: 約別有傳。

translations.literal: Yue separately has biography.
translations.idiomatic: Zu Yue has his own biography.

translations.idiomatic: Subheading: Zu Ti's elder brother Zu Na.

translations.literal: Na courtesy name Shiyan—most had moral conduct—able pure speech—literary meaning worth viewing.
translations.idiomatic: Zu Na, courtesy name Shiyan, was the most principled of the brothers; his Pure Conversation and essays impressed contemporaries.

sentences.zh: 性至孝，少孤貧，常自炊釁以養母，平北將軍王敦聞之，遺其二婢，辟爲從事中郎。

translations.idiomatic: Deeply filial, he grew up poor, cooked for his mother himself—Wang Dun gave him two maids and summoned him as administrative aide.

translations.literal: Successive offices many struck correct—had supplement to the times.
translations.idiomatic: In every post he corrected abuses and served the age.

translations.literal: Prince Qi Jiong raised righteous cause—Prince Zhao Lun seized Jiong's younger brother Prince Beihai Shi and former yellow gate gentleman Hongnong Dong Zuo's younger brother Ai—together with Jiong all rose—all were about harm them—Na submitted memorial rescue—together saw pardon.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Qi Sima Jiong raised the army of righteousness, Prince Zhao Sima Lun seized Sima Jiong's brother Prince of Beihai Sima Shi and Ai—brother of Hongnong gentleman Dong Zuo—who had risen with Jiong and were marked for death; Zu Na's memorial saved them all.

translations.literal: Afterward was central protector—heir apparent household superintendent—enfeoffed Duke of Jinchang.
translations.idiomatic: He became central protector and household superintendent to the heir, enfeoffed as duke of Jinchang.

translations.literal: Because Luoyang below about chaos—thereupon fled territory southeast.
translations.idiomatic: Foreseeing chaos in Luoyang he withdrew to the southeast.

translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yuan served as minister he named Zu Na libationer for army consultation.

translations.literal: "I hear ancients encountering fortune—then by merit extend their way—if they do not meet—then by words extend their way.
translations.idiomatic: "When ancient worthies met their hour they advanced the Way through deeds; when they did not, they advanced it through writing.

sentences.zh: 古必有之，今亦宜然。

translations.literal: Ancient surely had it—today also ought thus.
translations.idiomatic: So it was then and should be now.

sentences.zh: 當晉未有書，而天下大亂，舊事蕩滅，君少長五都，游臣四方，華裔成敗，皆當聞見，何不記述而有裁成？

translations.literal: When Jin not yet had histories—and realm great chaos—old affairs swept extinct—you young grew five capitals—traveled ministered four quarters—Chinese and barbarian rise fall—all ought heard seen—why not record narrate and have trim completion?
translations.idiomatic: Jin still lacks a standard history while the realm lies in ruins—memory fades. You grew up in the capitals and traveled the empire; you witnessed triumph and disaster among Chinese and barbarians alike—why not shape that into a chronicle?

sentences.zh: 應仲遠作《風俗通》，崔子真作《政論》，蔡伯喈作《勸學篇》，史遊作《急就章》，猶皆行於世，便成沒而不朽。

translations.literal: Ying Zhongyuan made Fengsu Tong—Cui Zizhen made Zheng lun—Cai Yong made Quan xue pian—Shi You made Ji jiu zhang—still all circulated in world—then became die yet not decay.
translations.idiomatic: Ying Shao's Fengsu Tong, Cui Yin's Zheng lun, Cai Yong's primer, Shi You's Ji jiu chapter—all lived after their authors and kept their names alive—why not you?

sentences.zh: 僕雖無才，非志不立，故疾沒世而無聞焉，所以自強不息也。

translations.literal: I although lack talent—not resolve then not establish—therefore hate die age without fame—thereby self strengthen without cease.
translations.idiomatic: I lack genius yet refuse aimlessness—I dread leaving life unheard—that keeps me striving.

sentences.zh: 況國史明乎得失之跡，俱取散悉，此可兼濟，何必圍棋然後忘憂也！

translations.literal: Moreover state history clarifies gain-loss traces—together gather scattered detail—this can aid both—why must weiqi then forget worry!
translations.idiomatic: National history clarifies right and wrong—salvaging scattered records serves court and countryside alike—you need not weiqi to banish sorrow!

translations.idiomatic: Zu Na sighed, "I do not reject your counsel—I lack the strength.

translations.literal: "—thereupon spoke it to emperor saying: "From antiquity small states still had historians—how much more great headquarters—how can not establish.
translations.idiomatic: He told the emperor, "Petty states kept historians—how can our great headquarters do without them?

sentences.zh: 」因舉隱，稱「清純亮直，學思沈敏，五經、群史多所綜悉，且好學不倦，從善如流。

translations.literal: "—thereupon recommended Yin—praised "pure honest bright straight—learning thought deep keen—five classics and collected histories much comprehended—and loves learning untiring—following good like flowing.
translations.idiomatic: He recommended Wang Yin as "pure, upright, learned across the classics and histories, tireless in study and quick to improve.

sentences.zh: 若使修著一代之典，褒貶與奪，誠一時之俊也。

translations.literal: If cause compile complete one generation's canon—praise blame grant seize—truly one generation's excellence.
translations.idiomatic: Entrust him with a chronicle of our age—judgment and verdict—and you gain the finest scholar of the hour.

translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked Zhong Ya, who answered, "Zu Na's nominee has talent for history, yet we cannot establish the office yet.

translations.literal: "—matter thereupon halted.
translations.idiomatic: The matter was dropped.

translations.literal: Yet historians' establishment—from Na began.
translations.idiomatic: Still, the push for historians began with Zu Na.

sentences.zh: 初，弟約與逖同母，偏相親愛，納與約異母，頗有不平，乃密以啟帝，稱：「約懷陵上之性，抑而使之可也。

translations.literal: Earlier—younger brother Yue together with Ti same mother—partially mutually intimate—Na and Yue different mother—somewhat had imbalance—thereupon secretly informed emperor—stating: "Yue harbors bullying-superiors nature—suppress and employ him acceptable.
translations.idiomatic: Zu Yue shared a mother with Zu Ti and was favored; Zu Na, born to another wife, nursed jealousy and secretly told the emperor, "Zu Yue would bully his sovereign—keep him low if you must.

sentences.zh: 今顯侍左右，假其權勢，將爲亂階」。

translations.literal: Now conspicuously serves left and right—lends him authority power—will become rebellion steps.
translations.idiomatic: Yet now he attends Your Majesty and wields power—that invites rebellion.

sentences.zh: 人謂納與約異母，忌其寵貴，乃露其表以示約，約憎納如仇，朝廷因此棄納。

translations.literal: People said Na and Yue different mother—jealous his favor nobility—thereupon exposed his memorial to show Yue—Yue hated Na like enemy—court therefore discarded Na.
translations.idiomatic: Critics called it stepbrother spite; someone leaked the memorial to Zu Yue, who hated Zu Na like an enemy, and the court cast Zu Na aside.

sentences.zh: 納既閒居，但清談、披閱文史而已。

translations.literal: Na once idle dwelt—but pure discourse—spread read literature and history only.
translations.idiomatic: Zu Na lived in retirement, debating Pure Conversation and reading histories.

sentences.zh: 及約爲逆，朝野歎納有鑒裁焉。

translations.literal: When Yue acted rebellious—court and wild sighed Na had judgment discernment.
translations.idiomatic: When Zu Yue rebelled, everyone conceded Zu Na's foresight.

sentences.zh: 溫嶠以納州里父黨，敬而拜之。

translations.literal: Wen Jiao because Na same province village father party—respected and bowed him.
translations.idiomatic: Wen Jiao, as an elder townsman, bowed to him in respect.

sentences.zh: 嶠既爲時用，盛言納有名理，除光祿大夫。

translations.literal: Jiao once was era employed—greatly spoke Na had name principle—appointed grand master of splendid happiness.
translations.idiomatic: Once back in office Wen Jiao praised Zu Na's philosophical clarity and had him named grand master of splendid happiness.

sentences.zh: 納嘗問梅陶曰：「君鄉里立月旦評，何如？

translations.literal: Na once asked Mei Tao saying: "Your village established monthly-dawn evaluation—how so?
translations.idiomatic: Zu Na once asked Mei Tao, "What of your village's first-of-month character reviews?

translations.literal: "—Tao said: "Praising good and censuring evil—that would be a fine rule.
translations.idiomatic: Mei Tao answered, "To praise virtue and blame vice—that would be an excellent method.

sentences.zh: 」納曰：「未益。

translations.literal: "—Na said: "Not yet beneficial.
translations.idiomatic: Zu Na said, "Not much improvement.

translations.literal: "—At the time Wang Yin was seated—thereupon said: "Shangshu states 'three years examine merit—three examinations demote and promote dark and bright'—how obtain one month then conduct praise blame!
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yin, present at the talk, said, "The Document states trials every three years across three cycles—how can judgment run every month?

sentences.zh: 」陶曰：「此官法也。

translations.literal: "—Tao said: "This is official law.
translations.idiomatic: Mei Tao replied, "That is the statute for officials.

translations.literal: Monthly dawn—private law.
translations.idiomatic: The first-of-month court is private opinion.

translations.literal: "—Speaking of houses—is that not office?
translations.idiomatic: When it speaks of houses, does it not mean offices?

translations.literal: Must accumulate long—good and evil then manifest—what difference public private!
translations.idiomatic: Merit and guilt emerge only after generations—what separates public from private judgment?

sentences.zh: 古人有言，貞良而亡，先人之殃；

translations.literal: Ancients had saying—chaste good yet died—forebears' calamity;
translations.idiomatic: The ancients said the loyal and good may still die—the fault lies with ancestors;

sentences.zh: 酷烈而存，先人之勳。

translations.literal: cruel fierce yet survive—forebears' merit.
translations.idiomatic: while the cruel may live on ancestral merit.

sentences.zh: 累世乃著，豈但一月！

translations.literal: Many generations then manifest—how only one month!
translations.idiomatic: Character shows across generations—not in a single month!

translations.idiomatic: Force monthly verdicts and Yan Hui gnawing dust looks corrupt;

translations.idiomatic: Sow at dawn and reap at dusk—good and evil have no time to show.

translations.literal: "—Tao and Ya together said "having divine awl—cannot obtain mallet".
translations.idiomatic: Mei Tao and Zhong Ya chorused, "A divine awl admits no mallet.

sentences.zh: 納曰：「假有神錐，必有神槌。

translations.literal: Na said: "If indeed divine awl—must have divine mallet.
translations.idiomatic: Zu Na answered, "Where there is a divine awl there is a divine mallet.

sentences.zh: 」雅無以對。

translations.literal: "—Ya had nothing with which reply.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong Ya had no reply.

sentences.zh: 卒於家。

translations.literal: Died at home.
translations.idiomatic: He died at home.

sentences.zh: 史評==

translations.literal: Heading marker 'Historians' judgment' with double equals in the Wikisource edition.
translations.idiomatic: Section heading: historians' judgment.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：劉琨弱齡，本無異操，飛纓賈謐之館，借箸馬倫之幕，當於是日，實佻巧之徒歟！

translations.literal: Historians say: Liu Kun weak age—originally lacked unusual conduct—flew tassel Jia Mi's lodge—borrow chopsticks Ma Lun's curtain—at that time—truly giddy clever fellows!
translations.idiomatic: The historians write: In youth Liu Kun cut no unusual figure—he flourished his silks in Jia Mi's salon and plotted at Prince Zhao's feast; in those days he was just another restless wit.

sentences.zh: 祖逖散穀周貧，聞雞暗舞，思中原之燎火，幸天步之多艱，原其素懷，抑爲貪亂者矣。

translations.literal: Zu Ti scattered grain relieving poor—heard cock dark danced—thought central plain's beacon fires—welcomed Heaven's march many hardships—trace his plain bosom—suppress call greedy turmoil ones.
translations.idiomatic: Zu Ti gave grain to the needy and danced to the midnight cock, longing for the burning Central Plain and greeting Heaven's hard trials—yet measured against his deeper bent he too chased profit amid chaos.

sentences.zh: 及金行中毀，乾維失統，三后流亡，遞縈居彘之禍，六戎橫噬，交肆長蛇之毒，於是素絲改色，跅弛易情，各運奇才，並騰英氣，遇時屯而感激，因世亂以驅馳，陳力危邦，犯疾風而表勁，勵其貞操，契寒松而立節，咸能自致三鉉，成名一時。

translations.literal: When metal line mid ruined—Heaven's cord lost governance—three queens drifted exile—successively wound Zhuli calamity—six Rong rampaged biting—mutually unleash long snake poison—thereupon plain silk changed color—slipshod changed emotion—each wielded strange talent—together soared heroic qi—met age hardship and stirred—because era chaos to gallop—displayed strength peril state—offended fierce wind yet showed firm—sharpened their chaste integrity—matched cold pine and established integrity—all able self-arrive three cords—complete reputation one generation.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jin mandate shattered and the heavenly axis broke, consorts wandered in exile and northern tribes ran riot like serpents—men of white silk turned gray and temperaments hardened: each seized the hour with soaring talent, sweating blood for a tottering court, braving gales to prove steadfast resolve and claiming the highest posts for a season.

sentences.zh: 古人有言曰：「世亂識忠良。

translations.literal: Ancients had saying: "Age chaos recognizes loyal good.
translations.idiomatic: The proverb says, "In chaos we know the loyal.

sentences.zh: 」益斯之謂矣。

translations.literal: "—indeed this speaks it.
translations.idiomatic: Surely it meant men such as these.

sentences.zh: 天不祚晉，方啟戎心，越石區區，獨-{御}-鯨鯢之銳，推心異類，竟終幽圄，痛哉！

translations.literal: Heaven not bless Jin—just opening Rong hearts—Yueshi petty alone {-yu-} whale young sharp—push heart alien kinds—ended dark prison—pain!
translations.idiomatic: Heaven withdrew favor from Jin and stirred barbarian ambition: Liu Kun alone faced leviathan foes, laid his heart before alien hosts, and ended in a traitor's jail—how bitter!

sentences.zh: 士稚葉跡中興，克復九州之半，而災星告釁，笠轂徒招，惜矣！

translations.literal: Shizhi stalked traces restoration—conquered recovered nine provinces' half—but disaster star announced rift—bamboo hat axle vain summoned—pity!
translations.idiomatic: Zu Ti strode through the revival and clawed back half the realm—yet ill stars foretold disaster and glory turned to ash: tragic!

sentences.zh: 贊曰：越石才雄，臨危效忠，枕戈長息，投袂徼功，崎嶇汾晉，契闊獯戎。

translations.literal: Encomium says: Yueshi talent heroic—faced peril displayed loyalty—pillow spear long sigh—fling sleeve seek merit—rugged Fen and Jin—parted long beside barbarian hosts.
translations.idiomatic: Encomium: Liu Kun towered in crisis and proved loyal—sleeping beside weapons he sighed away the nights, shook his sleeves into peril on Fen and Jin, and kept faith beside tribal allies.

sentences.zh: 見欺段氏，於嗟道窮！

translations.literal: Deceived by Duan clan—alas way exhausted!
translations.idiomatic: The Duan clan betrayed him—alas, his road ran out!

sentences.zh: 祖生烈烈，夙懷奇節。

translations.literal: Zu Sheng fierce fierce—early cherished strange integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Zu Ti burned with zeal and nursed rare honor from youth.

sentences.zh: 扣楫中流，誓清凶孽。

translations.literal: Strike oar midstream—swear clear fierce offspring.
translations.idiomatic: He struck his oar midstream and vowed to scourge the rebels.

sentences.zh: 鄰醜景附，遺萌載悅。

translations.literal: Neighboring uglies mirror attach—left sprouts carry joy.
translations.idiomatic: Neighbors rallied like shadows and scattered peoples rejoiced.

sentences.zh: 天妖是徵，國恥奚雪！

translations.literal: Heaven omens are signs—state shame how wipe!
translations.idiomatic: Yet Heaven sent dread signs—how could national shame be washed away?
